chapters.title: Chapter 5036: THE Infiniverse III
paragraphs: Noah had just finished waking Temporal, Eon, and Abaddon from their involuntary slumber.
The three of them were slowly regaining awareness, their foundations stabilizing after the unconsciousness forced upon them by Naldine’s display of THE Limitless Armature.
That glorious set of bones burning with THE Proterozoic Scale!
Temporal looked confused but functional, quickly coming back.

Eon seemed disoriented, her dark eyes flickering with awareness that was entirely her own for the first time in eons. Abaddon remained ashen, his hand still pressed against the chest where his Claim of Chaos no longer resided as he worked through it.
Noah stood and turned toward Temporal, preparing to give instructions for keeping watch over the other two while he and Naldine departed for wherever this Singular Cognizance supposedly waited.
"Keep an eye on them while I am gone. Make sure they do not do anything stu-"
BOOM!
A terrifying aura erupted from Noah’s body without warning.

It felt like a heavy and suffocating force pressing outward in all directions, reality itself groaning under pressure that radiated from his finite form. The multicolored rainfall of the Pluvial Epoch seemed to part around him, unable to fall through the density now emanating from his existence.

Temporal’s eyes rolled back immediately, his ancient form crumpling to the ground before he could even process what was happening. Eon collapsed beside him, her newly restored consciousness unable to withstand the pressure now flooding from Noah’s body. Abaddon fell last, his weakened foundations offering even less resistance than the others.
All three lay unconscious again, felled by whatever had just emerged from Noah’s existence.
Naldine looked toward him with cold gaze, her singularity-dotted eyes narrowing as she sensed something she clearly recognized.
"You...are still playing with Miniature Causes? One is not enough?"
Noah rose up with expression of genuine innocence, his hands raised in gesture of denial.
"It really was not me this time."
And it truly was not.
He could sense what THE Infiniverse had just done through their unbreakable connection, perceiving the aftermath of a Cause she had initiated alongside Ruination within his domain.
THE Hadean Emergence. Three Thousand Realms of Quintessence. A complete restructuring of everything THE Infiniverse contained, transforming her from vast domain into something unprecedented.
THE Seed of Observable Existence.
He couldn’t even complain to say why not a direct jump to Observable Existence because that would be far too grand. But...

The power of this transformation flowed through him because THE Infiniverse was an extension of his Existence rather than something separate. What she became, he partially became. What she achieved, he partially achieved. This was how their connection worked.
Her restructuring had created resonance through their connection that now pressed outward from his finite form with a force overwhelming anything at THE First Scale.
He had the authority of a Seed of Observable Existence flowing through him.

His finite existence somehow held up under this pressure, his foundations refusing to rupture despite containing force that should have exceeded what beings at his Scale could manage. But he could feel all this authority pressing onto something specific within him, concentrating on his Organ of Civilization surrounded by Quintessence Infiniforce.
An unfathomable process was beginning there.

He could not yet grasp what was happening, could not perceive the full scope of the transformation initiating within his foundations. But something was changing. Something was responding to the Seed’s authority flowing through him. Something was starting that would take time to complete.

For now, he controlled the terrifying pressure leaking from his existence, pulling it back within himself through will alone. The force receded, contained once more within his finite form rather than radiating outward to flatten everything nearby.
But his mind raced with possibilities.

His power paired with the power of THE Infiniverse. The Quintessence Infiniforce he generated internally combined with the authority of a Seed of Observable Existence. Could this combination violate existence itself?Could it potentially allow him to touch those unfathomable beings at THE Second Scale?

Before he made such a heavy claim, he would need to understand more about THE Proterozoic Scale. He would need to learn the mechanisms through which Second Scale beings operated, the vulnerabilities they possessed, the methodologies they employed.
He needed information that his current knowledge simply did not contain.
And hey, he had a walking, talking encyclopedia of information right here.

He turned to Naldine and smiled brilliantly, his heavy pressure now completely contained within his existence. She had knowledge accumulated across eons of operating at heights he was only beginning to perceive.
She looked back at him with cold expression that suggested his smile did not charm her in the slightest.
"One of these days, you will be wrong. Remember my warnings then."
Her voice held certainty.
"Do not keep messing around with Miniature Causes when your power cannot control what can happen. I will repeat that as many times as I need to."

She glanced down at the unconscious forms of Temporal, Eon, and Abaddon sprawled across the recovering landscape of Jotunheim. Her expression shifted to something approaching disdain as she observed three beings who had been felled twice in rapid succession by forces they could not withstand.
"For now, let us go."
She shook her head slowly while looking at the collapsed trio.
"Weak things that keep losing consciousness from pressure alone..."
She turned around and began walking, her Second Scale presence pressing against the multicolored rainfall as she moved.
Noah let Naldine leave first, watching her Second Scale presence carve a path through the multicolored rainfall as she departed.

Then he looked down at the three bodies sprawled before him. Temporal lay with purple temporal currents still flickering weakly around his form. Eon breathed slowly, her dark hair spread across the recovering ground of Jotunheim. And Abaddon remained ashen and hollow, his chest rising and falling with breaths that no longer carried the authority of Chaos.

An illusory consciousness separated from Noah’s current body, stepping out of himself like a shadow gaining substance. This fragment of his awareness moved toward the unconscious trio and sat down beside them, cross-legged amidst the multicolored rivers still flooding Jotunheim.
He placed his hand on Abaddon’s head and reached into the foundations of what remained.

His earlier sense was confirmed. The Claim of Chaos had not simply dissipated or dissolved. It had been taken, pulled through bonds that should not have permitted such transfer, claimed by someone who had been waiting for exactly this moment of weakness.
"Emotive."
His eyes flashed with chilly light as he thought about the Broken Doll he had spared not long ago. He had slapped her across existence and knocked out her teeth.
She had now grown very ambitious.
She had taken the Claim of Chaos itself, ascending from whatever she had been before to something that would require reevaluation. The manic entity...
Noah thought of many things as his consciousness remained beside the unconscious trio. He thought about many things.
He left this consciousness here to observe and protect while the three recovered.

His main body took a step and crossed vast distances, leaving Jotunheim behind to catch up with the walking, talking encyclopedia who had slowed her pace to wait for him, even though she never looked back.
In THE Infiniverse.
In THE Seed of Observable Existence.

Noah stood upon the golden sands of his Early Veiled Shore, observing a landscape transformed beyond what he remembered from his last visit. Abodes dotted the terrain now, structures of crystallized authority rising from foundations saturated with Quintessence Infiniforce. Hundreds of forming plots stretched across the shore.
It was oddly quiet and serene here.

Not many remained on the Early Veiled Shore at this moment, as most had been sent to THE Yggdrheim to undergo strengthening of their existence through adversity. The struggles occurring there would forge his people into something capable of surviving the conflicts spreading across Observable Existence. They would return transformed or they would not return at all.
Well, no, they would return!
The only one who happened to be here right now rose from a nearby plot of land.

Amelia Osmont brushed golden soil from her hands as she walked toward her son, her eyes already fixed on the skies above. She could instinctively sense the shocking changes that had taken place within this domain, her foundations resonating with transformations that affected everything dwelling within THE Infiniverse.
She was, after all, the mother of a finite being filled with glory!
She looked up and saw golden raindrops descending alongside rivers of multicolored brilliance cascading from heights that seemed infinite.
"Did you manage to pass a significant milestone?"
Noah smiled at his mother’s words, her ability to read situations never failing to remind him of where certain aspects of his own perception came from.
"Somewhat significant."
He watched the golden rain falling across the Early Veiled Shore, each droplet carrying Quintessence Infiniforce that would nourish whatever it touched.

"The things around me seem increasingly complex. They are not so simple like in the past. There is not a single enemy or ruler of a domain threatening us, but a collection of beings who lived for eons, each with their own schemes of what they want in existence."
He paused, considering how to explain conflicts that spanned Scales of power his mother could not yet perceive.
"We are just getting mixed up in them here and there, but I am riding the waves so far."
His mother nodded slowly, her expression holding the particular concern only parents could manage regardless of how powerful their children became.
She raised her hands to feel the raindrops of Quintessence Infiniforce landing on her palms, the multicolored authority absorbing into her foundations with each contact.
"Do not push yourself too much. I know you are pushing the others too so they can protect themselves, but take everything in strides. Focus on your farming, focus on your son."
Her expression shifted to something more mischievous.
"Maybe find me another daughter-in-law."
Noah shook his head at the ridiculous words.
"Come on. Let us see how our home is changing."

He waved his hand and multicolored light gathered before them, Quintessence Infiniforce condensing into physical form through will alone. A small boat materialized from the condensed authority, its hull burning with the same multicolored brilliance now filling his existence. The vessel floated above the golden sands, waiting for passengers.

Noah helped his mother board before stepping onto the boat himself. The moment his feet touched the deck, the vessel rose higher, lifting them above the Early Veiled Shore and carrying them outward toward the vastness now surrounding his farms.
What he saw was utter glory.

The Three Thousand Realms of Quintessence stretched across THE Infiniverse in configurations that defied easy comprehension. Each Realm blazed with distinct light declaring its unique nature, colors and authorities mixing.

The first Realm they approached shone with golden light carrying the essence of Dreams. It expanded outward endlessly like a flat plane of crystallized imagination, landscapes formed from concepts that only slumbering minds could perceive. Rivers of Infinity surged around its boundaries, connecting this Realm to others through waterways of conducted authority. Within its depths, Noah could see structures forming from pure potential, cities and forests and mountains emerging from the dream sands that now had physical reality.
His mother gasped beside him as their boat carried them past this first Realm toward another.

The second Realm burned with crimson-gold light of Helios, solar authority condensed into a region where fire and radiance served as natural law. Stellar bodies orbited within its expanse, suns of varying sizes and intensities providing illumination that would have blinded lesser beings. New suns and stellar bodies were being born...infinitely.
The heat emanating from this Realm pressed against their boat without threatening them, warmth recognizing its master and his mother as welcome rather than intruders.

They continued forward, and a third Realm came into view blazing with verdant light of Prana. Life authority saturated every aspect of this region, forests growing across surfaces that seemed to have no end.
Creatures moved through those forests, beings formed from pure vitality.

A fourth Realm shimmered with silver-blue light of Lunar essence, darkness and reflection mixing in configurations that created beauty through shadow rather than illumination. This Realm seemed quieter than the others, its authority more subtle, its gifts requiring contemplation to perceive.
A fifth Realm crackled with violet light of Apollyon, destructive potential contained within boundaries that prevented it from consuming everything nearby.

On and on they traveled, their boat carrying them through spaces between Realms where seas of Quintessence Infiniforce lapped against shores of condensed authority. Noah counted dozens of distinct configurations as they passed, each Realm unique, each one representing different aspects of existence given physical form.
The Realm of Manadynamics blazed with pure blue authority that reminded him of his earliest cultivation, Mana in its most fundamental expression saturating everything within.
The Realm of Apocalypse held configurations of ending and transformation, cycles of destruction and rebirth playing out across landscapes that seemed to change each time he looked away.
The Realm of Relativity bent around itself in ways that made his perception struggle, space and time operating according to rules that shifted based on the observer.
The Realm of Dreams continued expanding in the distance, its golden light now seeming like just one star among thousands filling the wonders of his domain.

His mother sat beside him in silence, her eyes wide with wonder. She had known her son was powerful. She had understood that he operated at heights she could not fully perceive. But seeing the scale of what he had built, what THE Infiniverse had become...
Her voice emerged soft against the vastness surrounding them.
"This is...beautiful."

He nodded without speaking, his attention fixed on the connections between Realms rather than the Realms themselves. Rivers of Infinity flowed between every configuration, conducted authority providing circulation that ensured no region existed in isolation. Seas of Quintessence Infiniforce filled the spaces between, generated authority from his own existence now serving as the medium through which everything connected.
The Primal Authority atmosphere saturated all of it, thick with combined Quintessence and Infinity that would empower any being breathing within this domain.

And still they traveled, their boat carrying them past the five hundredth Realm, the seven hundredth, the thousandth. Each one held unique characteristics. Each one provided different conditions for existence. Each one represented a piece of the vast architecture THE Infiniverse had constructed through her Hadean Emergence.
Noah’s eyes began shining with profundity as epiphany crystallized within his awareness.

He saw the Realms utilizing Infinity in configurations he had never considered. He observed how conducted authority enhanced environments rather than individual beings. He perceived the methodology through which external things could be bathed in endless potential without triggering THE Gamaidjan’s corruption.
"Infinity can be used in so many different ways."
He spoke to himself, his voice carrying revelation that pressed against his understanding of what he could accomplish.
"While the self is hard to bathe with Infinity, external things like Realms and Sacred Herbs are easier. The self risks corruption. But things outside the self have no identity to corrupt."
His eyes burned brighter as the implications expanded within his mind.

"And if I utilize Infinity even more, apart from herbs and Realms, so many things can be made Infinite. Armaments. Structures. Domains. Anything external to consciousness itself could potentially hold endless authority without suffering the consequences..."
HUUM!
The realization was one he already knew somewhat, but he could be more...comprehensive.
THE Infiniverse had integrated Infinity into her structure, into her Realms, into the environment itself rather than the consciousnesses dwelling within.
The environment could be Infinite without going mad.
The tools could be Infinite without losing identity.

Only the self required the careful progression that Naldine had described, the Anchoring and Transformation and eventual Transcendence that protected consciousness from corruption, and even that didn’t apply too much to him.

On a boat with his mother, Noah’s eyes burned with light of profundity as he toured his changing home. Three Thousand Realms stretched around them in every direction, a wonder built from Quintessence and Infinity that declared his domain something unprecedented in Observable Existence.
And he was only beginning to understand what it could become.

His earlier sense was confirmed.
The Claim of Chaos had not simply dissipated or dissolved.
It had been taken, pulled through bonds that should not have permitted such transfer, claimed by someone who had been waiting for exactly this moment of weakness.
"Emotive."
His eyes flashed with chilly light as he thought about the Broken Doll he had spared not long ago.
He had slapped her across existence and knocked out her teeth.
She had now grown very ambitious.
She had taken the Claim of Chaos itself, ascending from whatever she had been before to something that would require reevaluation.
The manic entity...
Noah thought of many things as his consciousness remained beside the unconscious trio.
He thought about many things.
He left this consciousness here to observe and protect while the three recovered.

His main body took a step and crossed vast distances, leaving Jotunheim behind to catch up with the walking, talking encyclopedia who had slowed her pace to wait for him, even though she never looked back.
In THE Infiniverse.
In THE Seed of Observable Existence.
Noah stood upon the golden sands of his Early Veiled Shore, observing a landscape transformed beyond what he remembered from his last visit.
Abodes dotted the terrain now, structures of crystallized authority rising from foundations saturated with Quintessence Infiniforce.
Hundreds of forming plots stretched across the shore.
It was oddly quiet and serene here.
Not many remained on the Early Veiled Shore at this moment, as most had been sent to THE Yggdrheim to undergo strengthening of their existence through adversity.
The struggles occurring there would forge his people into something capable of surviving the conflicts spreading across Observable Existence.
They would return transformed or they would not return at all.
Well, no, they would return!
The only one who happened to be here right now rose from a nearby plot of land.
Amelia Osmont brushed golden soil from her hands as she walked toward her son, her eyes already fixed on the skies above.
She could instinctively sense the shocking changes that had taken place within this domain, her foundations resonating with transformations that affected everything dwelling within THE Infiniverse.
She was, after all, the mother of a finite being filled with glory!
She looked up and saw golden raindrops descending alongside rivers of multicolored brilliance cascading from heights that seemed infinite.
"Did you manage to pass a significant milestone?"
Noah smiled at his mother’s words, her ability to read situations never failing to remind him of where certain aspects of his own perception came from.
"Somewhat significant."
He watched the golden rain falling across the Early Veiled Shore, each droplet carrying Quintessence Infiniforce that would nourish whatever it touched.
"The things around me seem increasingly complex.
They are not so simple like in the past.
There is not a single enemy or ruler of a domain threatening us, but a collection of beings who lived for eons, each with their own schemes of what they want in existence."
He paused, considering how to explain conflicts that spanned Scales of power his mother could not yet perceive.
"We are just getting mixed up in them here and there, but I am riding the waves so far."
His mother nodded slowly, her expression holding the particular concern only parents could manage regardless of how powerful their children became.
She raised her hands to feel the raindrops of Quintessence Infiniforce landing on her palms, the multicolored authority absorbing into her foundations with each contact.
"Do not push yourself too much.
I know you are pushing the others too so they can protect themselves, but take everything in strides.
Focus on your farming, focus on your son."
Her expression shifted to something more mischievous.
"Maybe find me another daughter-in-law."
Noah shook his head at the ridiculous words.
"Come on.
Let us see how our home is changing."
He waved his hand and multicolored light gathered before them, Quintessence Infiniforce condensing into physical form through will alone.
A small boat materialized from the condensed authority, its hull burning with the same multicolored brilliance now filling his existence.
The vessel floated above the golden sands, waiting for passengers.
Noah helped his mother board before stepping onto the boat himself.
The moment his feet touched the deck, the vessel rose higher, lifting them above the Early Veiled Shore and carrying them outward toward the vastness now surrounding his farms.
What he saw was utter glory.
The Three Thousand Realms of Quintessence stretched across THE Infiniverse in configurations that defied easy comprehension.
Each Realm blazed with distinct light declaring its unique nature, colors and authorities mixing.
The first Realm they approached shone with golden light carrying the essence of Dreams.
It expanded outward endlessly like a flat plane of crystallized imagination, landscapes formed from concepts that only slumbering minds could perceive.
Rivers of Infinity surged around its boundaries, connecting this Realm to others through waterways of conducted authority.
Within its depths, Noah could see structures forming from pure potential, cities and forests and mountains emerging from the dream sands that now had physical reality.
His mother gasped beside him as their boat carried them past this first Realm toward another.
The second Realm burned with crimson-gold light of Helios, solar authority condensed into a region where fire and radiance served as natural law.
Stellar bodies orbited within its expanse, suns of varying sizes and intensities providing illumination that would have blinded lesser beings.
New suns and stellar bodies were being born...infinitely.
The heat emanating from this Realm pressed against their boat without threatening them, warmth recognizing its master and his mother as welcome rather than intruders.
They continued forward, and a third Realm came into view blazing with verdant light of Prana.
Life authority saturated every aspect of this region, forests growing across surfaces that seemed to have no end.
Creatures moved through those forests, beings formed from pure vitality.
A fourth Realm shimmered with silver-blue light of Lunar essence, darkness and reflection mixing in configurations that created beauty through shadow rather than illumination.
This Realm seemed quieter than the others, its authority more subtle, its gifts requiring contemplation to perceive.
A fifth Realm crackled with violet light of Apollyon, destructive potential contained within boundaries that prevented it from consuming everything nearby.
On and on they traveled, their boat carrying them through spaces between Realms where seas of Quintessence Infiniforce lapped against shores of condensed authority.
Noah counted dozens of distinct configurations as they passed, each Realm unique, each one representing different aspects of existence given physical form.
The Realm of Manadynamics blazed with pure blue authority that reminded him of his earliest cultivation, Mana in its most fundamental expression saturating everything within.
The Realm of Apocalypse held configurations of ending and transformation, cycles of destruction and rebirth playing out across landscapes that seemed to change each time he looked away.
The Realm of Relativity bent around itself in ways that made his perception struggle, space and time operating according to rules that shifted based on the observer.
The Realm of Dreams continued expanding in the distance, its golden light now seeming like just one star among thousands filling the wonders of his domain.
His mother sat beside him in silence, her eyes wide with wonder.
She had known her son was powerful.
She had understood that he operated at heights she could not fully perceive.
But seeing the scale of what he had built, what THE Infiniverse had become...
Her voice emerged soft against the vastness surrounding them.
"This is...beautiful."
He nodded without speaking, his attention fixed on the connections between Realms rather than the Realms themselves.
Rivers of Infinity flowed between every configuration, conducted authority providing circulation that ensured no region existed in isolation.
Seas of Quintessence Infiniforce filled the spaces between, generated authority from his own existence now serving as the medium through which everything connected.
The Primal Authority atmosphere saturated all of it, thick with combined Quintessence and Infinity that would empower any being breathing within this domain.
And still they traveled, their boat carrying them past the five hundredth Realm, the seven hundredth, the thousandth.
Each one held unique characteristics.
Each one provided different conditions for existence.
Each one represented a piece of the vast architecture THE Infiniverse had constructed through her Hadean Emergence.
Noah’s eyes began shining with profundity as epiphany crystallized within his awareness.
He saw the Realms utilizing Infinity in configurations he had never considered.
He observed how conducted authority enhanced environments rather than individual beings.
He perceived the methodology through which external things could be bathed in endless potential without triggering THE Gamaidjan’s corruption.
"Infinity can be used in so many different ways."
He spoke to himself, his voice carrying revelation that pressed against his understanding of what he could accomplish.
"While the self is hard to bathe with Infinity, external things like Realms and Sacred Herbs are easier.
The self risks corruption.
But things outside the self have no identity to corrupt."
His eyes burned brighter as the implications expanded within his mind.
"And if I utilize Infinity even more, apart from herbs and Realms, so many things can be made Infinite.
Armaments.
Structures.
Domains.
Anything external to consciousness itself could potentially hold endless authority without suffering the consequences..."
HUUM!
The realization was one he already knew somewhat, but he could be more...comprehensive.
THE Infiniverse had integrated Infinity into her structure, into her Realms, into the environment itself rather than the consciousnesses dwelling within.
The environment could be Infinite without going mad.
The tools could be Infinite without losing identity.

Only the self required the careful progression that Naldine had described, the Anchoring and Transformation and eventual Transcendence that protected consciousness from corruption, and even that didn’t apply too much to him.
On a boat with his mother, Noah’s eyes burned with light of profundity as he toured his changing home.
Three Thousand Realms stretched around them in every direction, a wonder built from Quintessence and Infinity that declared his domain something unprecedented in Observable Existence.
And he was only beginning to understand what it could become.

chapters.title: Chapter 5037: Innovators and Destroyers I
paragraphs: Among the vast reserves of knowledge THE Mnemonic Leviathan had accumulated since its emergence under THE Beholder, certain patterns repeated themselves across eons of observation.

Beings fell into categories regardless of their power or their Scale, regardless of their Civilizations or their ambitions. Some built. Others burned. The distinction defined more about their nature than any classification ever could.

THE Infiniverse and its Master belonged among the Innovators of Observable Existence. The ongoing forging of Three Thousand Realms showed architecture unprecedented in recorded memory. Innovation required vision that destruction never demanded.

THE Creature stood among the greatest Innovators THE Mnemonic Leviathan had ever catalogued. Humble origins as a Primordial Architect had given way to something defying classification entirely, a being who had shattered what he was to become what no one else had become.
What he built, what he represented, what he had achieved through methodology no other Primordial Architect had dared attempt, all of it spoke to innovation refined across existence itself.
And then there were those who destroyed.
Horus existed within the Leviathan’s reserves of knowledge as a destroyer of considerable accomplishment. His methodologies claimed countless beings who could not resist what he wielded.
Yet when measuring pure lethality, when calculating bodies dissolved and existences ended, Horus was not the worst the Leviathan had knowledge of.
Among the worst destroyers was a Singular Cognizance that THE Mnemonic Leviathan had met alongside its Progenitor eons before THE Infinite Unfurling reshaped everything.
THE Beholder had led them to a region of Observable Existence where something terrible was being tested, and there they had encounteredMalachar, THE Extinction Artificer.
That Singular Cognizance had been experimenting in engineering a virus capable of inflicting existence itself.
Not beings and certainly not Civilizations, but Existence.

Malachar had designed weavings of destruction so precise that they could target the fundamental nature of what something was rather than simply ending what something did. And it had tested this engineered horror against an entire group of beings born from the intersection of differentiation and undifferentiation, ancient entities known asAntediluvian Oneswho had existed since shortly after THE First Cause imposed structure upon chaos.
All Antediluvian Ones inflicted with this engineered weaving had perished.

Those at THE First Scale had died screaming as their existence unraveled from within. Those at THE Second Scale had died more slowly, their greater foundations providing only prolonged suffering rather than survival.
Every single one touched by Malachar’s creation had ceased to exist, their classifications and their power meaningless against destruction designed specifically to unmake them.
There were many destroyers across Observable Existence. Horus, Erwin, Renne, and Beowulf and many others whose names filled the Leviathan’s reserves with records of atrocity and ending.

But Malachar, THE Extinction Artificer, would undoubtedly be considered among the more accomplished ones. If ever that Singular Cognizance engineered something similar against Undivided Ones or Primordial Architects, would any remain today? Would Observable Existence itself survive such targeted annihilation?

THE Mnemonic Leviathan had once asked THE Beholder regarding who would ultimately prove most accomplished in Observable Existence. Its Progenitor had considered the question with attention rarely granted to anything, that singular eye processing variables across eons of accumulated observation.
THE Beholder’s answer had been simple.

Those who destroy always had an easier time accomplishing their weavings. To unmake required only force and precision. To create required vision and patience and understanding that destruction never demanded. A child could tear down what masters spent lifetimes building.
To destroy was much easier than to innovate.

Innovators or destroyers. Builders or burners. Those who pushed existence toward greater complexity or those who pulled it back toward the simplicity of undifferentiation. THE Mnemonic Leviathan slumbered now within one of the boundlessly forming Realms inside THE Infiniverse, its ancient form resting amidst innovation unprecedented in its reserves of knowledge.
It wondered, as consciousness drifted through memories spanning eons, just what type of beings would end up on top.
Would the Innovators prevail through creations that outlasted those who built them?
Or would the destroyers simply unmake everything before innovation could complete its work?
The answer remained unwritten, and THE Mnemonic Leviathan found that uncertainty more fascinating than any knowledge it had already accumulated.
—Reflections of THE Mnemonic Leviathan, recorded during slumber within THE Seed of Observable Existence
As Noah continued his journey across the Three Thousand Realms of his home, he came across an entire Realm holding the composition of none other than Muspelheim.
Vibrant flames and weavings of immensity permeated throughout this region, crimson-gold authority radiating from structures that had been integrated into THE Infiniverse’s new architecture.
He was about to steer the boat past this Realm when he heard that heavy voice call out to him.
A certain pink dolphin’s tone pressed against his awareness from within the flames, lazy and unhurried as always yet somehow demanding attention regardless.
Noah smiled and steered the multicolored boat toward the fiery crimson-gold Realm.

The vessel carried him and his mother through boundaries separating configurations, crossing from the space between Realms into the heart of reformed Muspelheim itself. Heat pressed against them immediately. The flames parted as Noah’s authority declared his sovereignty over everything within this domain.

A massive crimson-gold mountain dominated the center of this Realm, its slopes releasing flows of lava burning with Quintessence Infiniforce rather than simple molten rock. The liquid authority cascaded down its sides in rivers that would have dissolved anything lacking sufficient foundations, pooling at the base in lakes of concentrated power.

In the center of that lava, a crystalline crimson-gold tree irradiated immense heat that pressed against perception itself. Its branches reached toward heights that seemed infinite within this Realm, its roots drinking deep from the molten authority surrounding it. The tree pulsed with life that had nothing to do with biology and everything to do with power given vegetative form.
And basking within the lava beside that tree, lounging with laziness that seemed impossible given the environment, floated the massive form of a pink dolphin.
THE Mnemonic Leviathan.
Noah had called this ancient entity into his home so he could steal, ahem, obtain its knowledge.
The Leviathan possessed reserves of information accumulated across eons of existence.
He nodded toward the pink dolphin as his boat came to rest near the edge of the lava pool.
"Do you have something new to share? I was in the middle of profundities and epiphanies."
The Mnemonic Leviathan’s massive form shifted slightly within the molten authority, one eye opening to regard Noah with attention that belied its lazy posture.
"I was just dreaming about Innovators and destroyers. Contemplating which type of being would ultimately prevail across Observable Existence."
The dolphin’s voice rumbled through the Realm, somehow audible despite the crackling of flames all around.
"But I also had to ask something. My Progenitor has sent word to check my status. Is it acceptable to speak about where we are located?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5038: Innovators and Destroyers II
paragraphs: Noah frowned at such words.
The location of his home was a secret for reasons. Overly powerful beings could not be simply told or given the coordinates of where he was.
"Who is your Progenitor? What Scale of existence are they in?"
THE Mnemonic Leviathan paused before answering, its massive form settling deeper into the lava as if the question required consideration despite having an obvious answer.

"They should be on THE Second Scale. Known as THE Beholder. A Singular Cognizance, though you may not understand what that classification means. It refers to entities that emerged during the age of nothingness before differentiation taught existence how to have boundaries. Singular Cognizances predate most of what currently lives, their perspectives shaped by observing..."
The pink dolphin had begun to ramble on with its explanation, but Noah’s eyes had already widened with surprise.
THE Beholder?

THE Beholder had helped him not too long ago. He had not expected any connection between that ancient entity and this lazy, good-for-nothing pink dolphin lounging in his lava pools. Well, both loved to observe.
His eyes shone brilliantly as he interrupted the Leviathan’s rambling.
"How deeply are you and THE Beholder connected?"
The pink dolphin seemed almost pleased by the question.
"Few in existence inherited the weavings of the distant observer. THE Beholder seeded portions of itself across eons..."
The Leviathan’s voice grew more formal as it discussed its origins.

"Myself and THE Baboon of Wisdom were the only two to successfully stem from the weavings of THE Beholder. We carry portions of our Progenitor’s accumulated observation within our foundations, serving as extensions of its awareness across regions it cannot directly perceive."
There was also a Baboon of Wisdom?
A baboon and a dolphin. Existence was truly unique in the configurations it produced.

Noah thought about this revelation for a moment. Naldine was moving with one of his bodies as she sought for them to meet a Singular Cognizance aligned with their interests. If he could have a friendly Singular Cognizance like THE Beholder potentially come to him, why not?
"Tell THE Beholder exactly where you are and who you are with."
His words emerged as command rather than request.
"Let your Progenitor know that THE Youngest has built something unprecedented within Observable Existence, and that THE Beholder is welcome to observe it firsthand."
The Mnemonic Leviathan’s eyes gleamed with something approaching excitement despite its lazy demeanor.
"It will be done."

Noah nodded at the confirmation before turning his attention toward the crystalline tree rising from the center of the lava pool. Its crimson-gold branches pulsed with authority accumulated since THE Hadean Emergence first triggered, a Sacred Plant that had formed alongside everything else within the reformed Infiniverse.
He emerged from the boat and walked across the surface of the lava. His mother remained behind, watching her son approach the tree with curiosity.

Noah reached the tree’s base and looked upward at branches spreading across heights that seemed to contain their own infinities. One particular branch caught his attention, smaller than its siblings but pulsing with intensity.
He waved his hand.

The branch separated from the tree without resistance, cutting itself free at his command and floating down toward his waiting palm. The moment his fingers closed around it, heat flooded through his awareness alongside prompts materializing before his vision.
|Item Acquired|
|Name: Ember Branch of the Hadean Tree|

|Origin: First Sacred Flora to emerge during THE Hadean Emergence within THE Seed of Observable Existence. Crystallized from concentrated Quintessence Infiniforce and primordial fire authority during the formation of the Three Thousand Realms.|

|Description: A branch severed from the Hadean Tree, containing authority sufficient to function as weapon against Civilizations at Fundamental Depth. Strikes from this branch carry primordial fire that burns foundations rather than flesh, damaging the structure of what beings have built rather than merely their physical forms. Can greatly wound Fundamental Depth entities and their Civilizations through direct contact.|
Noah smiled at the details as profundities continued swirling through his mind.

He had infused Infinities into a Sacred Herb before, and the process had allowed him to smoothly transition from Countable to Uncountable. The methodology worked. External objects could contain endless authority without suffering THE Gamaidjan’s corruption because they lacked consciousness to corrupt.
So what if he filled Infinity into an item like this branch?
"Flow. Flow gloriously."
He whispered calmly to the branch, his voice carrying command that reality itself would obey.

In the next moment, vibrant multicolored waves of Quintessence Infiniforce flooded from his body. The internally generated authority poured into the branch without resistance, filling its crystalline structure with endless potential that expanded rather than contained. Infinity from Observable Existence joined the Quintessence, conducted authority merging with generated authority within the branch’s foundations.
The process was instant.
The process was boundless.
The process was complete before Noah could fully perceive what he had accomplished.
BOOM!

A pillar of multicolored brilliance erupted from Noah’s hand, continuing upward across the entire Realm of reformed Muspelheim. The light pressed against the boundaries separating this configuration from others, declaring that something unprecedented had just occurred within THE Seed of Observable Existence.
In his hands, the branch had transformed.

It pulsed and shook with authority that seemed barely contained within its crystalline form. Auroras of Infinity symbols swirled around its length, endless loops declaring the nature of what now filled this weapon. The pressure radiating from it alone was terrifying, force leaking from its surface despite Noah’s grip attempting to contain what he had created.
New prompts materialized before his vision.
|Infinity Armament Forged|
|Name: THE Hadean Infinibrand|
|Classification: First Infinity Armament forged under THE Youngest|

|Origin: Ember Branch of the Hadean Tree infused with boundless Quintessence Infiniforce and conducted Infinity from Observable Existence. Represents the first successful integration of endless authority into weaponized form.|

|Primary Capability: Can infinitely strike any Civilization with equivalent force that most Absolute Depth entities cannot withstand. Each strike carries the full pressure of Infinity compressed into physical impact, damaging foundations in ways that regeneration cannot easily address.|

|Secondary Capability: Can only be wielded by someone possessing understanding of or relation to Infinity. Beings lacking such connection will find the Armament refusing their grasp, its authority rejecting those unworthy of conducting what it contains.|

|Tertiary Capability: Endlessly generates Infinity within its structure, accumulating authority that can be unleashed all at once for strikes vastly exceeding normal output. The longer the Armament is held without attacking, the greater the force of its eventual release.|
|Limitation: Minimal effectiveness against anything at THE Proterozoic Scale.|
Noah looked at his latest innovation, THE Hadean Infinibrand pulsing in his grip as Infinity continued generating within its crystalline form.
He nodded slowly.

Naldine had told him much about THE Proterozoic Scale, about the methodologies those beings employed and the transformations they underwent to wield Infinity safely. The gap was fundamental rather than quantitative.
But gaps could be bridged through innovation rather than simple accumulation.

In addition to his already burning and widespread Infinity, if he also decked himself with Infinity Armaments among other things, he could bridge that gap slowly. Not through single overwhelming power, but through accumulated advantages that stacked until the gap became navigable. Weapons that struck with Infinity. Armor that deflected with Infinity. Tools that manipulated with Infinity. Environments that supported with Infinity.
Layer upon layer upon layer until even Proterozoic Scale entities would be...reachable.

As all of this happened, he continued paying attention to his Organ of Civilization surrounded by Quintessence Infiniforce. The transformation of THE Infiniverse was affecting something within him, the immensity flowing throughout his existence pressing against that particular aspect of his foundations. Something was changing there, responding to his domain becoming a Seed of Observable Existence.
He simply did not know what it was transforming into.
Not yet.

By the time he turned around, the Hadean Infinibrand still pulsing in his grip, he saw his mother talking with the slumbering pink dolphin. THE Mnemonic Leviathan had shifted position to better face Amelia, answering all her questions calmly while she sat at the edge of the lava pool with curiosity.
Noah smiled at the scene.

Existence was truly unique in the configurations it produced.
Noah thought about this revelation for a moment.
Naldine was moving with one of his bodies as she sought for them to meet a Singular Cognizance aligned with their interests.
If he could have a friendly Singular Cognizance like THE Beholder potentially come to him, why not?
"Tell THE Beholder exactly where you are and who you are with."
His words emerged as command rather than request.
"Let your Progenitor know that THE Youngest has built something unprecedented within Observable Existence, and that THE Beholder is welcome to observe it firsthand."
The Mnemonic Leviathan’s eyes gleamed with something approaching excitement despite its lazy demeanor.
"It will be done."
Noah nodded at the confirmation before turning his attention toward the crystalline tree rising from the center of the lava pool.
Its crimson-gold branches pulsed with authority accumulated since THE Hadean Emergence first triggered, a Sacred Plant that had formed alongside everything else within the reformed Infiniverse.
He emerged from the boat and walked across the surface of the lava.
His mother remained behind, watching her son approach the tree with curiosity.
Noah reached the tree’s base and looked upward at branches spreading across heights that seemed to contain their own infinities.
One particular branch caught his attention, smaller than its siblings but pulsing with intensity.
He waved his hand.
The branch separated from the tree without resistance, cutting itself free at his command and floating down toward his waiting palm.
The moment his fingers closed around it, heat flooded through his awareness alongside prompts materializing before his vision.
|Item Acquired|
|Name: Ember Branch of the Hadean Tree|
|Origin: First Sacred Flora to emerge during THE Hadean Emergence within THE Seed of Observable Existence.
Crystallized from concentrated Quintessence Infiniforce and primordial fire authority during the formation of the Three Thousand Realms.|
|Description: A branch severed from the Hadean Tree, containing authority sufficient to function as weapon against Civilizations at Fundamental Depth.
Strikes from this branch carry primordial fire that burns foundations rather than flesh, damaging the structure of what beings have built rather than merely their physical forms.
Can greatly wound Fundamental Depth entities and their Civilizations through direct contact.|
Noah smiled at the details as profundities continued swirling through his mind.
He had infused Infinities into a Sacred Herb before, and the process had allowed him to smoothly transition from Countable to Uncountable.
The methodology worked.
External objects could contain endless authority without suffering THE Gamaidjan’s corruption because they lacked consciousness to corrupt.
So what if he filled Infinity into an item like this branch?
"Flow.
Flow gloriously."
He whispered calmly to the branch, his voice carrying command that reality itself would obey.
In the next moment, vibrant multicolored waves of Quintessence Infiniforce flooded from his body.
The internally generated authority poured into the branch without resistance, filling its crystalline structure with endless potential that expanded rather than contained.
Infinity from Observable Existence joined the Quintessence, conducted authority merging with generated authority within the branch’s foundations.
The process was instant.
The process was boundless.
The process was complete before Noah could fully perceive what he had accomplished.
BOOM!
A pillar of multicolored brilliance erupted from Noah’s hand, continuing upward across the entire Realm of reformed Muspelheim.
The light pressed against the boundaries separating this configuration from others, declaring that something unprecedented had just occurred within THE Seed of Observable Existence.
In his hands, the branch had transformed.
It pulsed and shook with authority that seemed barely contained within its crystalline form.
Auroras of Infinity symbols swirled around its length, endless loops declaring the nature of what now filled this weapon.
The pressure radiating from it alone was terrifying, force leaking from its surface despite Noah’s grip attempting to contain what he had created.
New prompts materialized before his vision.
|Infinity Armament Forged|
|Name: THE Hadean Infinibrand|
|Classification: First Infinity Armament forged under THE Youngest|
|Origin: Ember Branch of the Hadean Tree infused with boundless Quintessence Infiniforce and conducted Infinity from Observable Existence.
Represents the first successful integration of endless authority into weaponized form.|
|Primary Capability: Can infinitely strike any Civilization with equivalent force that most Absolute Depth entities cannot withstand.
Each strike carries the full pressure of Infinity compressed into physical impact, damaging foundations in ways that regeneration cannot easily address.|
|Secondary Capability: Can only be wielded by someone possessing understanding of or relation to Infinity.
Beings lacking such connection will find the Armament refusing their grasp, its authority rejecting those unworthy of conducting what it contains.|
|Tertiary Capability: Endlessly generates Infinity within its structure, accumulating authority that can be unleashed all at once for strikes vastly exceeding normal output.
The longer the Armament is held without attacking, the greater the force of its eventual release.|
|Limitation: Minimal effectiveness against anything at THE Proterozoic Scale.|
Noah looked at his latest innovation, THE Hadean Infinibrand pulsing in his grip as Infinity continued generating within its crystalline form.
He nodded slowly.
Naldine had told him much about THE Proterozoic Scale, about the methodologies those beings employed and the transformations they underwent to wield Infinity safely.
The gap was fundamental rather than quantitative.
But gaps could be bridged through innovation rather than simple accumulation.
In addition to his already burning and widespread Infinity, if he also decked himself with Infinity Armaments among other things, he could bridge that gap slowly.
Not through single overwhelming power, but through accumulated advantages that stacked until the gap became navigable.
Weapons that struck with Infinity.
Armor that deflected with Infinity.
Tools that manipulated with Infinity.
Environments that supported with Infinity.
Layer upon layer upon layer until even Proterozoic Scale entities would be...reachable.
As all of this happened, he continued paying attention to his Organ of Civilization surrounded by Quintessence Infiniforce.
The transformation of THE Infiniverse was affecting something within him, the immensity flowing throughout his existence pressing against that particular aspect of his foundations.
Something was changing there, responding to his domain becoming a Seed of Observable Existence.
He simply did not know what it was transforming into.
Not yet.
By the time he turned around, the Hadean Infinibrand still pulsing in his grip, he saw his mother talking with the slumbering pink dolphin.
THE Mnemonic Leviathan had shifted position to better face Amelia, answering all her questions calmly while she sat at the edge of the lava pool with curiosity.
Noah smiled at the scene.

chapters.title: Chapter 5039: Conviction! I
paragraphs: Naldine had observed Primordial Architects across eons of coexistence at THE Second Scale, and she had learned to read them within moments of meeting.

Some projected power through displays meant to intimidate. They blazed with their Civilizations at every opportunity, announced their presence through pressure that crushed everything nearby, demanded acknowledgment through force that left no room for alternative responses.

These were the weak ones. They required external validation because internal certainty eluded them. Beowulf fell into this category despite his accomplishments. Horus as well. Their need to be seen as powerful revealed the hollow spaces within their foundations where true conviction should have resided.
Others operated through silence and observation, moving through existence without announcing themselves, accomplishing objectives before anyone realized they had arrived.

These possessed greater strength than the loud ones, but their quietness often stemmed from fear rather than confidence. They avoided confrontation because uncertainty plagued them. They gathered information obsessively because they doubted their ability to adapt without preparation.
THE Arboreal Warden Yggvaros demonstrated this quality, powerful beyond question yet forever waiting, forever watching, forever hesitating before the decisive moments that might define his legacy.
The truly strong existed in neither category.

They did not need to project because projection implied audience. They did not need to hide because hiding implied threat. They simply were what they were, their existence radiating conviction so fundamental that doubt could find no purchase within their foundations.

THE Creature embodied this quality more completely than any being Naldine had encountered. That entity did not announce his power or conceal it. He simply existed, and existence bent around him because his certainty about what he was exceeded reality’s certainty about what it was.
The strongest psychological quality an existence could possess was not power. It was not intelligence. It was not even wisdom accumulated across eons of careful observation.
It was conviction about one’s own existence.

The absolute, unshakeable certainty that you were exactly what you believed yourself to be. That your path was correct not because evidence supported it but because you walked it. That your Civilization represented truth not because others agreed but because you had built it from foundations that could not be questioned.

This conviction served as THE Civilizational Anchor that THE Proterozoic Scale demanded. Without it, Infinity’s whispers found cracks to exploit. Without it, THE Gamaidjan convinced its victims that they were something other than what they had believed. The truly strong never fell to such corruption because corruption required uncertainty to begin its work, and they possessed none.
When Naldine looked at Osmont, she saw this conviction leaking from his existence like light escaping a star too bright for its shell.

He did not merely possess confidence. He radiated it with intensity that pressed against everything nearby, declaring his certainty about what he was and what he would become without requiring words to announce it.

Every action he took emerged from foundations so assured of their own nature that doubt seemed like a foreign concept his consciousness. But...he also seemed to have doubt sometimes as it was odd. Paradoxical really.
She was almost envious.
Almost.

Her own conviction had been forged across eons of careful cultivation, tested against countless challenges that had shattered lesser certainties, refined until it could withstand pressures that crushed Primordial Architects less prepared than herself. She had earned her confidence.
Osmont seemed to have simply been born with it as he was too young.

Or perhaps his journey through existence had compressed eons of testing into years that somehow produced equivalent results. Either way, he possessed the quality in abundance that most Second Scale beings spent lifetimes attempting to develop, and he wielded it without apparent awareness of how rare it was.
But Naldine also knew that strength could become weakness through simple excess.

Conviction that never bent would eventually shatter when faced with truths it could not incorporate. Certainty that never questioned would miss dangers that uncertainty would have caught. Those playing with Infinity required flexibility alongside their foundations, the ability to adapt when endless potential revealed aspects of existence their confidence had not anticipated.
Osmont’s conviction was immense.
She simply hoped it was not so rigid that it would break rather than bend when Infinity finally showed him something his certainty could not accept.
Across THE Interstices.
As she was thinking all of this, Naldine looked toward Osmont and noticed he seemed to have a particularly content expression right now.

They had moved from Alfheimr into the gray expanse of endless weavings, that liminal space where boundaries blurred and travel between configurations became possible. The multicolored rain of the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity passed around them in rivers that painted the gray with borrowed brilliance, his Miniature Cause still reshaping Observable Existence even as they traveled through it.
She asked with genuine curiosity coloring her tone.
"What made you so happy?"
Osmont’s smile carried satisfaction that seemed entirely inappropriate given everything that was happening.
"I have just forged my first Infinity Armament. If I make enough of them paired with the rest of my power, maybe I can begin thrashing a Proterozoic Scale Being."
His eyes gleamed as he continued.
"Unless you want to let me study the bones in your arm a little. Who knows, maybe I can begin forming Proterozoic Bones or Organs even before attaining THE Proterozoic Scale."
There was that endless confidence and conviction again, as if his words would no doubt become reality soon enough.
Naldine wanted to shake her head, but ultimately she found herself responding with something other than dismissal.
"You are filled with unknowns, so who knows. Maybe you are right."
She paused, letting her next words carry the full measure of her accumulated experience.
"But do not underestimate any Proterozoic Scale Being. Even someone like Beowulf is impossible for you to defeat right now, and he is one among many of the weaker ones."
Her singularity-dotted eyes fixed on him with intensity that most beings would have found uncomfortable.

"You do not know much and have not heard much about Primordial Architects and how many there are, yes? Often times, existence rarely rewards the clamorous. There are those who believe that to be heard is to be powerful. They shout their intentions to the rafters, rattling their Civilizations to mask the hollow thrum of their own fear. Those are beings like Beowulf."
She gestured at the multicolored rain surrounding them.

"They are like a summer storm, all thunder and sudden flashes of light, yet they spend their fury in a single frantic moment, leaving nothing behind but damp existence and silence. Such loudness and volume is not strength."
Her voice lowered as she continued.

"The truly dangerous do not broadcast their malice. They cultivate it in stillness. While the fool boasts, the most terrifying enemies are those who have mastered the patience of years. They are silent, analyzing the very threads of your life, finding the single strand that, if pulled, causes your entire Civilization to unravel."
Naldine let those words settle before delivering the point she truly wanted him to understand.

"By the time you feel their touch upon your throat, the trap was sprung eons ago. Fear the shadow that does not move, for it is calculating exactly how to break you before you even know you are at war. Those are the Primordial Architects and Singular Cognizances for you to worry about. The ones you will not know the names of before they try to destroy you."

She spoke at length and in detail because she truly wanted him to learn and grow, wanted him to develop some caution that might keep him alive long enough to reach the potential she saw within his foundations. Everything she said came from eons of watching brilliant beings die because they underestimated enemies they never saw coming!
And yet even after she said all that, he gazed at her with the same conviction and a smile as he asked his next question.
"Might you happen to know of these silent schemers and planners that are supposed to not even be known? Maybe I can also scheme against them."
Naldine took a moment as she sighed internally. This one truly was something else entirely.
"To scheme against such forces is to attempt to outrun your own shadow."
She considered how much to reveal, how much warning would actually penetrate that impenetrable confidence.
"When it comes to if I know of these silent architects... I do. I know some. But others are really silent, and even I do not know them."
Her expression grew more serious than it had been throughout their journey together.

"You must be cautious of the names Sammael and Ishara. Nasty and cautious beings. But if you seek the true horizon of your undoing, you must look to the two who have moved beyond mere planning. They are the ones who will succeed in collapsing everything you hold dear if you are not careful, for they have already achieved the impossible."
She held up one finger.

"First, fear Eqono, THE Bright. He does not walk alone. He has bound the wills of multiple Primordial Architects to his cause, turning Architects into his own personal instruments. It is whispered that he possesses multiple Proterozoic Organs and Bones, foundations forged beyond what most at our Scale have accomplished."
A second finger rose.

"Second, and perhaps most terrifying, is Cyndane. She does not bother with a choir of followers. She has formed an alliance with the Singular Cognizances themselves, entities that predate differentiation. She carries THE Proterozoic Sight, an eye that sees not what is, but the inevitability of what must cease to be."
Naldine let her hand fall as she delivered the final truth.

"And these are just the ones I have gathered information about. The ones even I do not know about are the really scary ones for you. It is why I really am trying my best here. I know you actually face an impossible wall."
After saying such words, she looked at him closely again.

Would he pause? Show some concern, any hint of fear crossing those features that seemed immune to such emotions? She had just described beings who could end everything he cared about, forces that had already achieved what most considered impossible, enemies who would not announce themselves before striking.
She watched.
And she saw him smile again with that same conviction, as if what he heard changed nothing whatsoever about his approach or his confidence.
Naldine found that she could say nothing more to scare him.

His conviction was unbreakable, it seemed. Either that quality would carry him to heights even she could not imagine, or it would shatter against truths that refused to bend regardless of how certain he was about his own nature.
She genuinely did not know which outcome awaited him.

chapters.title: Chapter 5040: Conviction! II
paragraphs: While Naldine and Osmont crossed THE Interstices.
In the Lands of the Dead.

The Living had their spotlight while the dead shone in the endless shadow behind them. This was the natural order of existence, the balance that most never perceived because they were too focused on the brightness of life to notice the vast darkness stretching infinitely beyond it.
THE Dead Order knew this more than others.

She had not been given her spotlight to shine for eons, remaining behind the scenes while lesser beings claimed glory that should have been hers. Her weavings had been collapsed, her authority diminished, her very existence reduced to something that required rescue rather than inspiring fear. But now, her time was coming. THE Creature had restored her, elevated her, granted her power that finally matched the grandeur she had always deserved.
She wanted pain and vengeance against all those who went against her.

But frustratingly enough, the most recent one was the one THE Creature had forbidden her from pursuing. Apparently now called THE Youngest rather than the nothing he had been when she first encountered him. Osmont!
Him and Sigrid, these defilers of Order who had nearly collapsed the last shred of her weavings, were the ones THE Creature told her to forget about entirely.
If she wanted vengeance, she could decide the fate of THE Living Paradox who had collapsed her first eons ago.
But that felt like a consolation prize. A leftover offered to quiet a child’s tantrum rather than genuine acknowledgment of the wrongs done to her.
She shook her head in frustration as she looked around at her current surroundings.

She stood atop an intricate obsidian temple positioned at the peak of a massive white mountain, hazy white clouds drifting past its edges like ghosts too timid to approach. This was her domain, the Lands of the Dead that she had claimed and cultivated across eons of careful work.
And inside this temple, she was not alone.

An entity entirely humanoid in nature sat on a mat near the temple’s edge, sipping tea as if visiting someone’s home for casual conversation rather than intruding upon a domain she had no right to occupy.
Dark blue hair cascaded down her shoulders in waves that seemed to absorb what little light existed within the temple. Ancient eyes held depths. Her beauty was calm and undeniable.

She stared out across the expanse of obsidian and white all around them while multicolored rivers and rain surged outside the temple’s boundaries. Some streams of that multicolored rain flowed directly across the temple floor, the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity touching even this realm of death with its transformative authority.
Part of this rain was his power. THE Creature’s power.

THE Dead Order focused on the woman who had not said a single word to her since appearing here uninvited. Since she was here, it meant THE Creature had allowed her to be here. But...the silence had stretched past tolerance into outright insult, this stranger treating her like furniture rather than the master of this domain.
She finally brought herself to ask with irritation bleeding through her tone.
"Who might you be? You come into my domain and you do not even bother to speak to me."

The entity opposite her looked over with expression suggesting the question barely warranted acknowledgment. She shook her head slowly, as if deciding whether responding was even worth the effort, before her voice emerged with calm that bordered on dismissive.

"The Lands of the Dead are not something you had built the fence and hung the gate yourself. It is a quaint delusion, the arrogance of a child claiming the sea because he has managed to wet his feet."
She sipped her tea before continuing.

"I was breathing when the first Undivided One was a mere whisper in the dark, long before the threads of your little weaving were even conceived. I have stood before entities whose claims to the Lands of the Dead are written in foundations older than your entire lineage, beings who have forgotten more of ending than you will ever learn."
Her ancient eyes fixed on THE Dead Order with something approaching pity.
"To me, you are a flickering candle of emotions and death. You have no domain here, little one. You have only a temporary reprieve from the silence."
THE Dead Order looked over incredulously at the words that had just been spoken to her.
What the fuck?
What the FUCK?!

Who was this bitch that THE Creature brought over to think she could talk to her like this?! She had been healed and elevated by THE Creature himself, her power now standing at Absolute of THE First Scale!
She was untouchable! If Osmont stood before her again, maybe if he groveled sufficiently, she might spare him the full measure of her vengeance.
But this bitch?!

THE Dead Order rose up as her full chest heaved up and down, rage building within her foundations as she prepared to demonstrate exactly why she was not someone to be dismissed so casually. Her authority began gathering around her, death and weavings of Order responding to her fury as she was about to erupt when...
SAA!
Another aura entered the temple.

A calm and scholarly visage appeared at the temple’s entrance, a figure she recognized. Anaximander arrived drenched in the multicolored rain, droplets of Quintessence Infiniforce and Infinity sliding off his form as he stepped inside. His eyes moved first to THE Dead Order with her rage-twisted expression, then to the entity calmly sipping tea whose ancient eyes actually lit up with warmth when he arrived.
Anaximander looked at the enraged face of THE Dead Order and blinked with an expression suggesting genuine surprise.
"Were you just about to go against one of the more powerful Second Scale Primordial Architects in Observable Existence? You have stronger conviction than I do, O Dead Order!"
THE Dead Order paled as her figure almost stumbled backward.
THE Second Scale? Primordial Architect? That woman?
The rage drained from her foundations faster than it had gathered.
She had no words as she watched that entity nod toward Anaximander with a genuine smile, familiarity passing between them as if they were old acquaintances reuniting after long separation.
"It has been a while, Jokul."
The Primordial Architect then turned her head to glance at THE Dead Order before speaking with calm that made every word cut deeper than intended insult could have.

"I do not know why THE Creature attached himself to something as vain as this during his rebirth. She is a creature of vanity and jealous whims, propping up a hollow existence with the fragile scaffolding of her own emotions."
She sipped her tea again.
"She possesses neither the depth nor the clarity to ever reach THE Second Scale. Such petty passions are but smoke. They will carry her nowhere in the vastness of existence."
A slight shrug.
"But who am I to judge? Where is the big guy? Is he still fighting Horus?"

THE Dead Order actually stumbled backward this time, rage and humiliation warring within her as she stared at this supposed Primordial Architect who had just dissected her entire existence. What the fuck was her problem?!
At her words, Anaximander smiled.
"Nice to see you too, Tairiyya. Try to be nicer."
He moved to sit near her, accepting tea she poured without being asked.
"And THE Creature is wrapping things up. What do you think of the Miniature Cause of rain outside? The one who induced it alongside THE Creature is also a friend of mine."
Anaximander and Tairiyya spoke casually about matters spanning Scales and eons, their conversation flowing as if they had not just dismissed someone standing right before them.
They forgot or ignored THE Dead Order completely, her presence in her own domain rendered irrelevant by beings whose existence operated on levels she could not touch.
She stood there, hollow and humiliated, wondering if anything she achieved would ever matter to those who truly held power in Observable Existence.

sentences.text: While Naldine and Osmont crossed THE Interstices.
In the Lands of the Dead.
The Living had their spotlight while the dead shone in the endless shadow behind them.
This was the natural order of existence, the balance that most never perceived because they were too focused on the brightness of life to notice the vast darkness stretching infinitely beyond it.
THE Dead Order knew this more than others.
She had not been given her spotlight to shine for eons, remaining behind the scenes while lesser beings claimed glory that should have been hers.
Her weavings had been collapsed, her authority diminished, her very existence reduced to something that required rescue rather than inspiring fear.
But now, her time was coming.
THE Creature had restored her, elevated her, granted her power that finally matched the grandeur she had always deserved.
She wanted pain and vengeance against all those who went against her.
But frustratingly enough, the most recent one was the one THE Creature had forbidden her from pursuing.
Apparently now called THE Youngest rather than the nothing he had been when she first encountered him.
Osmont!
Him and Sigrid, these defilers of Order who had nearly collapsed the last shred of her weavings, were the ones THE Creature told her to forget about entirely.
If she wanted vengeance, she could decide the fate of THE Living Paradox who had collapsed her first eons ago.
But that felt like a consolation prize.
A leftover offered to quiet a child’s tantrum rather than genuine acknowledgment of the wrongs done to her.
She shook her head in frustration as she looked around at her current surroundings.
She stood atop an intricate obsidian temple positioned at the peak of a massive white mountain, hazy white clouds drifting past its edges like ghosts too timid to approach.
This was her domain, the Lands of the Dead that she had claimed and cultivated across eons of careful work.
And inside this temple, she was not alone.

An entity entirely humanoid in nature sat on a mat near the temple’s edge, sipping tea as if visiting someone’s home for casual conversation rather than intruding upon a domain she had no right to occupy.
Dark blue hair cascaded down her shoulders in waves that seemed to absorb what little light existed within the temple.
Ancient eyes held depths.
Her beauty was calm and undeniable.
She stared out across the expanse of obsidian and white all around them while multicolored rivers and rain surged outside the temple’s boundaries.
Some streams of that multicolored rain flowed directly across the temple floor, the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity touching even this realm of death with its transformative authority.
Part of this rain was his power.
THE Creature’s power.
THE Dead Order focused on the woman who had not said a single word to her since appearing here uninvited.
Since she was here, it meant THE Creature had allowed her to be here.
But...the silence had stretched past tolerance into outright insult, this stranger treating her like furniture rather than the master of this domain.
She finally brought herself to ask with irritation bleeding through her tone.
"Who might you be?
You come into my domain and you do not even bother to speak to me."
The entity opposite her looked over with expression suggesting the question barely warranted acknowledgment.
She shook her head slowly, as if deciding whether responding was even worth the effort, before her voice emerged with calm that bordered on dismissive.
"The Lands of the Dead are not something you had built the fence and hung the gate yourself.
It is a quaint delusion, the arrogance of a child claiming the sea because he has managed to wet his feet."
She sipped her tea before continuing.
"I was breathing when the first Undivided One was a mere whisper in the dark, long before the threads of your little weaving were even conceived.
I have stood before entities whose claims to the Lands of the Dead are written in foundations older than your entire lineage, beings who have forgotten more of ending than you will ever learn."
Her ancient eyes fixed on THE Dead Order with something approaching pity.
"To me, you are a flickering candle of emotions and death.
You have no domain here, little one.
You have only a temporary reprieve from the silence."
THE Dead Order looked over incredulously at the words that had just been spoken to her.
What the fuck?
What the FUCK?!
Who was this bitch that THE Creature brought over to think she could talk to her like this?!
She had been healed and elevated by THE Creature himself, her power now standing at Absolute of THE First Scale!
She was untouchable!
If Osmont stood before her again, maybe if he groveled sufficiently, she might spare him the full measure of her vengeance.
But this bitch?!
THE Dead Order rose up as her full chest heaved up and down, rage building within her foundations as she prepared to demonstrate exactly why she was not someone to be dismissed so casually.
Her authority began gathering around her, death and weavings of Order responding to her fury as she was about to erupt when...
SAA!
Another aura entered the temple.
A calm and scholarly visage appeared at the temple’s entrance, a figure she recognized.
Anaximander arrived drenched in the multicolored rain, droplets of Quintessence Infiniforce and Infinity sliding off his form as he stepped inside.
His eyes moved first to THE Dead Order with her rage-twisted expression, then to the entity calmly sipping tea whose ancient eyes actually lit up with warmth when he arrived.
Anaximander looked at the enraged face of THE Dead Order and blinked with an expression suggesting genuine surprise.
"Were you just about to go against one of the more powerful Second Scale Primordial Architects in Observable Existence?
You have stronger conviction than I do, O Dead Order!"
THE Dead Order paled as her figure almost stumbled backward.
THE Second Scale?
Primordial Architect?
That woman?
The rage drained from her foundations faster than it had gathered.
She had no words as she watched that entity nod toward Anaximander with a genuine smile, familiarity passing between them as if they were old acquaintances reuniting after long separation.
"It has been a while, Jokul."
The Primordial Architect then turned her head to glance at THE Dead Order before speaking with calm that made every word cut deeper than intended insult could have.
"I do not know why THE Creature attached himself to something as vain as this during his rebirth.
She is a creature of vanity and jealous whims, propping up a hollow existence with the fragile scaffolding of her own emotions."
She sipped her tea again.
"She possesses neither the depth nor the clarity to ever reach THE Second Scale.
Such petty passions are but smoke.
They will carry her nowhere in the vastness of existence."
A slight shrug.
"But who am I to judge?
Where is the big guy?
Is he still fighting Horus?"
THE Dead Order actually stumbled backward this time, rage and humiliation warring within her as she stared at this supposed Primordial Architect who had just dissected her entire existence.
