chapters.title: Chapter 5041: Nakatsukuni! I
paragraphs: Anaximander settled more comfortably near Tairiyya, his scholarly demeanor relaxing in the presence of someone he clearly considered an equal.
"One after another, things are becoming more and more chaotic out there."
His voice carried observation rather than complaint.

Tairiyya sipped her tea and sighed, her ancient eyes turning toward the vibrant multicolored rain cascading past the temple’s boundaries. The Pluvial Epoch painted everything with borrowed brilliance, authority from sources she understood all too well saturating even this realm of death.
"For eons, it was quiet. For eons, the stillness was absolute. Everybody just worked hard for their weavings."
She set her cup down with deliberate care.

"But now, the first dominoes have been tipped by hands that should not have the reach to touch them. The Peasant, THE Creature, and even the Infinity-bearer have begun to move, their frantic shuffles triggering a cascade that cannot be halted."
Her expression grew more contemplative as she continued.

"Because of them, the Primordial Architects have stirred with activity. Even the Singular Cognizances, those who have spent an eternity as mere Observers, are beginning to step from the shadows of the void."
A sound escaped her that might have been a laugh in someone less ancient.

"Ah. In the end, this will lead to a ruin more absolute than the dark. In all of existence, there are few who truly know what they are doing. The rest are simply shouting into the abyss, unaware that the abyss is finally preparing to answer."
She glanced at Anaximander with something approaching fondness.
"Things are about to get really wild, Jokul. I am not sure if even THE Creature understands."
At such words, Anaximander smiled with an expression suggesting he knew things that even this Primordial Architect might not have considered.
"I think out of many existences in, well, Existence, THE Creature is one of the rare few that do understand. But yes, it will be unpredictable."
He paused before asking his next question with careful precision.
"Can you give me a gauge of just how much of a pull you and other Primordial Architects feel toward the one who bears and utilizes Infinity more freely than all of you at THE Proterozoic Scale?"
Tairiyya’s ancient eyes sharpened at the question, her cup freezing halfway to her lips before she set it down entirely.
"How much of a pull we have?"
A laugh escaped her.

"Hah, Jokul, you have been gone for too long. Infinity is everything and nothing. It is the only thing we have, as THE Primordial Source is too far, too unknown. We cannot even begin to approach it while Infinity flows throughout Observable Existence, tantalizingly close yet requiring transformations most cannot survive."
She stared directly at him now.

"The others will come at him relentlessly. Not out of malice, though some will cloak their hunger in righteous purpose. They will come because they must. Because Infinity calls to those of us who have spent eons preparing to receive it, and he walks around conducting it as if breathing air. Do you understand what that means to beings who have sacrificed everything for even a fraction of what he wields carelessly?"

Jokul was silent at this, his scholarly demeanor fading into something more somber. He looked out into the rain, that endless multicolored cascade reshaping Observable Existence through authority his friend had triggered alongside THE Creature.

He raised his hand to feel THE Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity, letting droplets land upon his palm. The sensation was unlike anything else in existence, power that declared endless potential ready for those capable of receiving it.
He sighed with sound carrying understanding that words could not express.
And this whole time, nobody said a word to THE Dead Order standing behind them.
She remained there, forgotten entirely, her existence rendered irrelevant by a conversation about matters so far beyond her that she could barely comprehend what was being discussed.
Her domain. Her temple. Her supposed moment of restored glory.
And she was fucking furniture.
Naldine Manthon continued to move across the Interstices because her destination was truly far.

The gray expanse stretched endlessly around them, multicolored rain from the Pluvial Epoch painting borrowed brilliance across spaces that normally held none. She had traveled these paths many times across her existence, but never with someone quite like the entity floating beside her. Young. Impossibly young by any standard that mattered. Yet somehow wielding authority that beings at her Scale spent eons trying to obtain!
She turned to Osmont as she continued speaking.
"When I ask myself how I can best prepare you, knowledge is the best thing for someone as young as you. I will share this freely."
Her singularity-dotted eyes fixed on him with intensity that most would have found uncomfortable.
"The enemies you face at THE Proterozoic Scale will be extremely powerful. You should understand their power somewhat. So I will tell you about THE Proterozoic Scale itself."

Osmont looked at her and gave a nod of expectation, his expression carrying that same unshakeable conviction she had observed again and again. He listened like someone who expected to eventually surpass whatever she described rather than someone preparing to face impossible odds.
Naldine continued without waiting for verbal acknowledgment.

"Infinity is something those at THE Second Scale chase, but it is not always their foremost power. It is an unfathomable force, but just like THE Primordial Source, if you do not have access to it, then you do not."
She let that settle before proceeding.

"THE Proterozoic Scale stands by itself even without Infinity. After you have set your Civilizational Anchor, many things become possible. Those who have done so are consideredRhyacian Proterozoic Lifeforms."
Her voice took on the cadence of utter glory and wonder as they continued ahead!

"Above them areTHE Calymmian Proterozoic Lifeforms. And the distant, out of reach level for many at THE Second Scale isTHE Ediacaran Proterozoic Lifeform.Rhyacian, Calymmian, and Ediacaran. That is the known scope of THE Second Scale."

chapters.title: Chapter 5042: Nakatsukuni! II
paragraphs: Osmont listened calmly as they continued through the gray expanse before asking his question.
"You would not happen to be at the Calymmian Proterozoic Scale or Ediacaran, would you? This would make things very easy."
Naldine looked back at him and did not reply.
She simply stared out toward where they were going, letting silence serve as answer enough.
After a moment, she continued as if the question had never been asked.
"Rhyacian Proterozoic Lifeforms alone are a problem for you. If we put Beowulf on the lowest tier, someone could be stronger than him by a factor of ten and still be a Rhyacian Proterozoic Lifeform."
She glanced at him to ensure he understood the scale of what she was describing.
"As I mentioned, Infinity and THE Primordial Source are ideal. But because they can be so distant, most of us focus on what is Observable and Unobservable. We take that into our Civilizations."
Her explanation shifted into something more fundamental.

"All of existence divides into two categories. The Observable and the Unobservable. Everything that can be perceived, measured, witnessed, or acknowledged falls into the Observable. Everything that cannot falls into the Unobservable."
She gestured at the gray Interstices around them.

"The Observable is what you currently see, what can be seen, what has been seen, what will be seen. The accumulated force of all potential perception pressing against existence from every angle. When something enters the Observable, it gains substance through acknowledgment. It becomes real in ways that unwitnessed things are not."
Her voice grew more contemplative as she described the counterpart.

"The Unobservable is not simply what you cannot see. It is what exists beyond the possibility of perception. What has never been witnessed and never will be. The vast darkness surrounding everything acknowledged, pressing inward with force that dwarfs what the Observable contains. For every star that shines, countless more burn in regions no consciousness will ever reach."
She watched his expression for signs of comprehension before continuing.
"At THE Proterozoic Scale, we learn to draw from both. We infuse and integrate the force of all that is Observable, or the force of all that is Unobservable, into our existence."
The technical details came easily to her after eons of living them.

"Those accomplished enough can form Proterozoic Bones or Organs even without the infusion of Infinity, if they fill them with enough weavings of either Observable or Unobservable. After they have transformed enough of their existence, when they pass a certain marker, they go from Rhyacian Proterozoic Lifeforms to Calymmian Proterozoic Lifeforms."

She explained as best she could because she knew the stakes involved. There were beings at the Calymmian Proterozoic Scale who would very much like to put their hands on this infinite battery floating beside her. Knowledge might be the only thing keeping him alive when those beings eventually made their moves.
And after all this talking...
HUUM!
She finally felt them nearing their destination as white-gold light flickered at the edges of the gray expanse.

They finished crossing the Interstices as Naldine wrapped her authority around both of them and took a single step. Instantly, the two of them appeared in an endless field of white stretching in every direction without boundary or feature, a space between spaces where nothing existed until permission was granted.
Naldine voiced out commandingly with her authority pressing into the blankness.
"Naldine Manthon."
HUUM!

After stating her name in this endless white space, existence flickered once more as brilliant verdant light wrapped around the two of them. The white dissolved into color and sensation and the feeling of somewhere specific rather than nowhere at all.
They found themselves standing on vibrant plains.

Naldine did not much care for natural beauty after eons of witnessing it across countless regions of Observable Existence, but she could appreciate the craftsmanship here nonetheless as this place...was built and carved by someone. The grass beneath their feet held coloring so rich it seemed painted rather than grown, emerald blades swaying in breezes that carried warmth without humidity. Distant mountains rose against skies holding shades of blue that deepened toward purple at the horizons, their peaks touched by mists.
Away from these plains stood a massive and glorious set of structures.
The buildings ahead followed architectural principles that prioritized harmony with their surroundings rather than dominance over them.

Traditional designs built with natural materials, timber and stone and clay arranged uniquely. Gently sloping tiled roofs curved upward at their edges, their surfaces glazed in colors that shifted between gray and blue depending on how light struck them. Wooden pillars supported overhanging eaves providing shelter and shade, their surfaces aged to warm browns that spoke of centuries rather than years.
The structures connected through courtyards and covered walkways, each building relating to its neighbors in configurations designed for wonder.
Some courtyards held gardens of carefully arranged stones and pruned trees. Others held ponds reflecting the sky above with clarity that made their surfaces seem like windows into inverted worlds.
The layout showed simplicity and organic growth guided by consistent principles, each addition respecting what came before while contributing something new to the whole.
Naldine began walking toward the structures as Osmont fell into step beside her.
"Welcome to a domain hidden between spaces, between Observable and Unobservable. Welcome to Nakatsukuni."
She glanced at him with an expression suggesting her next words were not optional.
"Do not do anything crazy here as...well, you can sense and see it."

He should not do anything crazy because as they neared the structures, Noah could sense ans see what she meant. The figures and auras of hundreds of terrifying First Scale entities at the level of Absolutes pressed against his awareness from various buildings and courtyards, apex beings who would have been considered overwhelming threats in any other context.
And...a few Proterozoic Scale entities added their presence to the collective force, their authority making THE First Scale beings seem dim by comparison.
And above all of them, the brilliance of one that stood supreme here blazed like a sun among candles!
That...should be the Singular Cognizance!

chapters.title: Chapter 5043: Nakatsukuni! III
paragraphs: Nakatsukuni.
Noah looked at the place they had arrived at, and it was a marvel in several different ways.

The primary entrance rose before them like a declaration of intent made physical. A large heavy wooden gate stood at the center, its surface adorned with iron ring handles and ornate carvings depicting scenes he could not immediately interpret. This was no ordinary gateway but something built higher than the surrounding roofline, its very elevation announcing the significance of what lay beyond.

Stone and clay walls flanked the entrance in configurations that seemed both defensive and decorative. Gray roof tiles topped these barriers in patterns matching what he could see of the main structures deeper within, creating visual harmony. Everything here felt intentional, every stone placed with purpose, every tile arranged.
At the gateway itself, Noah saw something that made even his composed expression shift slightly.

Two Primordial Architects of THE First Scale stood guard, both at the level of Absolutes, their presence pressing against his awareness with force that would have crushed lesser beings simply through proximity. They turned to look at Naldine Manthon first, offering nods of recognition that suggested familiarity. Then their attention shifted to him.
Their eyes shone with luminosity that seemed to pierce through whatever he presented on the surface.

Both entities were humanoid in nature, their forms draped in wrappings of shining white and pink that moved like living things despite the absence of wind. Their faces held beauty that transcended simple aesthetics, features arranged according to proportions that seemed mathematically perfect in ways mortal minds struggled to quantify. Ancient eyes regarded him from those beautiful faces.
Even though they were Absolute, a million trash bum Absolutes like THE Living Elemental could stand before them, and all would get thrashed silly.
Naldine only nodded to them and passed through the gate without breaking stride.

Noah went inside as well, stepping through the massive entrance and immediately finding himself in a courtyard. It stretched before him as a communal hub connecting all the interior living quarters. Beyond this space, the actual buildings rose on raised foundations of stone and wood, elevated to protect from ground moisture and requiring visitors to step up when entering.

Deep curved wooden eaves extended over every entryway, providing shade and protection while framing views of the sky from positions within the courtyard. The architecture felt alive in ways that stone and wood should not feel, as if the structures themselves were aware of who passed through them.
Noah smiled as he spoke to Naldine walking ahead of him.
"After all the warnings you have given me, you have brought me to a place filled with Primordial Architects. Has this all just been a long elaborate trap?"
His tone carried amusement rather than genuine concern.
Naldine continued forward without looking back as she replied.

"I brought you here because I am confident I can protect you here. Barring anything unexpected happening, this should be a good step forward for you if we can secure the promises of the one we came to see."
Barring any unexpected happenings.

Noah sighed internally at these words because they felt like a very bad flag that Naldine had just planted. Existence loved to be filled with unexpected happenings. The moment someone expressed confidence that nothing would go wrong, the foundations of reality itself seemed to take that as a challenge.
Inside, Noah saw something that genuinely surprised him.

Undivided Ones and Formless Terrors swept the extended courtyards with brooms and brushes, their movements methodical and unhurried. Some of these beings stood taller than normal humanoids, their bodies wrapped in stellar crimson skin that seemed to contain galaxies within its depths.
Others bore obsidian skin so dark that light seemed to fall into it and never return. Still others blazed with white stellar skin, their forms radiating illumination that pressed against perception.
All of them swept.

Was this their meditation? Some instructed method to elevate their Civilizations given by the Singular Cognizance who oversaw this place? Noah never expected to see Undivided Ones and Formless Terrors sweeping grounds like normal humans performing household chores. The sight seemed almost absurd given the power contained within each of these entities.
Every single one turned to see him and Naldine as they crossed through the courtyard.

Noah felt every single gaze stay on him, dozens of ancient consciousnesses tracking his movement through their domain. They did not stop their sweeping. They did not approach or threaten. They simply watched, their attention pressing against his awareness like physical force that accumulated with each additional observer.
In one area they passed, Noah saw something even more unexpected.

A Primordial Architect at THE Proterozoic Scale sat at a table playing chess with three other Primordial Architects. The Second Scale being moved a piece with fingers that seemed too elegant for the simple action, pale skin catching light in ways that made it seem luminescent rather than merely fair.

Long silver-gold hair cascaded down his back in waves that moved with supernatural grace, framing aristocratic features that belonged on sculptures rather than living faces. Dark elegant clothing wrapped his slender frame, the garments suggesting nobility from traditions Noah did not recognize.
When they passed, the game stopped entirely.
Noah and this Proterozoic Scale entity locked eyes across the courtyard.

The being smiled dangerously, lips curving upward to reveal the faintest hint of sharpened teeth. One pale hand rose in a wave toward Noah, the gesture carrying mockery beneath its apparent friendliness.
Noah mimicked the same smile and waved back without hesitation.
The moment he did so, the smile disappeared from that Primordial Architect’s face. Those aristocratic features sharpened into something predatory as eyes that had been amused became cutting.
Naldine’s voice cut through the tension.
"Remember, do not try anything over the top. Strangers are allies until they become enemies, and things can change rather quickly. Let us go."
As if she expected trouble might start from that exchange alone, her authority wrapped around them again. She took a step, and they appeared before the tallest building in this place.
Two THE Proterozoic Scale Primordial Architects sat beside the entrance, both adorned in garments similar to the guards they had seen at the main gate.

The first seemed extremely young despite the ancient depths within her eyes. Silver-white hair fell past her shoulders in straight lines that caught light like silk threads woven from moonlight. Her features held delicacy that suggested fragility while her presence declared anything but weakness.

She sipped tea with movements so economical they seemed rehearsed across centuries of repetition, her small form somehow containing authority that pressed against Noah’s awareness despite her apparent youth.
The second Primordial Architect sat in a meditative position beside her, and he was anything but delicate.

A massive humanoid demon with crimson-gold horns curving from his temples regarded Noah and Naldine with calm that seemed inappropriate for something so obviously built for violence. His skin held the color of dried blood, stretched over a frame that towered even while seated. He smiled, the expression somehow warm despite the fangs it revealed, and his deep voice echoed out across the courtyard.
"Naldine Manthon. You have come bearing gifts and catastrophes."
The words pressed against everything nearby.
"Why would you bring such a thing when you know The Leader does not want any conflicts? By simply bringing you and him here, you force The Leader’s hand."

Noah looked at this Primordial Architect and the one beside him. Their power felt heavy and suffocating to him even now, pressing against his foundations with force that reminded him exactly how far he still had to go. But he could not help marveling at all of this despite the pressure.
There were peaceful groups of Primordial Architects under a Singular Cognizance?

Existence continued to be vast and grand beyond measure. He had assumed beings at these heights existed in constant conflict, scheming against each other across eons while pursuing power through any means available. Yet here stood evidence of cooperation, of community, of entities choosing peace over perpetual warfare.
As he was thinking this, Naldine looked at the two Primordial Architects blocking their path. She nodded toward them.
"Sabayne. Ba’alzan. Times are changing."
Her voice carried conviction that pressed back against the force the demon had projected.

"Even those who hold peace as their only prayer will find the silence shattered. When the conflict breaks, peace becomes a cage, not a sanctuary. No soul remains a mere observer as all of us are forced to move when the foundations shift."
Her singularity-dotted eyes blazed brighter.
"The times of peace are over."
BOOM!
With such words, Naldine Manthon pushed the doors of the structure before them open.

Inside, a heavy aura pulsed outward, the presence of a Singular Cognizance that reminded Noah of the brilliance he had felt when THE Beholder manifested. This was another entity from before differentiation, another consciousness that had observed existence since before Observable Existence learned how to be observable, they held an authority so absolute it made everything outside feel like a fleeting dream!

chapters.title: Chapter 5044: Nakatsukuni! IV
paragraphs: The structure they entered was dim and filled with an atmosphere resembling outer space itself.

Sparkling stellar lights sprinkled all around them in configurations that seemed random until Noah looked closer and recognized patterns within the chaos. Constellations formed and dissolved in the darkness, galaxies spiraling in miniature across surfaces that should have been walls but felt more like windows into the void between stars.
The entity inside acted as a source of profound light amidst this manufactured cosmos.

Noah observed a white-blue singularity contained within a constantly shifting square cube. The singularity pulsed with brilliance that reminded him immediately of THE Beholder, that same sense of consciousness predating differentiation, that same feeling of being observed by something that had witnessed existence learn how to exist.
But where THE Beholder had felt distant and evaluating, this presence felt vast in ways that pressed against his awareness with force unlike any other Proterozoic Scale entity.
They were a powerful fucker!
When they entered, this entity had its singularity gaze fixed directly on him.

The gaze felt calm and curious rather than hostile, the attention of something genuinely interested rather than threatened. Noah met that observation without flinching, his foundations steady despite the pressure emanating from a being that had likely observed THE First Cause itself.
Naldine looked up toward this entity as she began to speak.
"Out of all the Singular Cognizances and Primordial Architects who have carved their names into the foundations of reality, you are the only one who has managed to remain truly unaligned, Sadakar."
She paused, her singularity-dotted eyes reflecting the sun-like brilliance of the entity before them.
"But even here, tucked between the Observable and the Unobservable, you cannot claim ignorance. Both of us have felt and listened to the tremors in the weavings, the echoes of THE First Cause."

Noah remained silent, his gaze fixed on the shimmering silhouette of the Leader. This was Naldine’s negotiation to conduct. He was here as the one being discussed rather than the one doing the discussing, at least for now. And he was gathering more and more information before he began to act as there were many questions.
How many more places like these were there? Clusters of Primordial Architects- were they similar to here or smaller or larger?
"Those who hold peace would surely side with those who do not seek the Splintering of Observable Existence," Naldine continued, her tone shifting from observation to cold pragmatic proposal.
"I did not bring him here to hide him. I came to introduce the two of you and to form a treaty."
She gestured toward Noah, her hand steady despite the presence pressing against everything in this space.

"A pact of mutual defense. Because when the monsters who wish to return everything to nothingness and endless potential finally make their move, even Nakatsukuni will be forced to choose a side. I would prefer you choose the side that allows existence to continue existing."

The Singular Cognizance pulsed before them, its contained brilliance fluctuating as it processed her words. That ancient gaze shifted between Naldine and Noah, evaluating both with attention that seemed to perceive far more than surfaces could reveal.
Finally, it began to speak in a voice deep enough to resonate through one’s foundations.

"Existence...is an unfathomable weaving of immensity, a discordant symphony of a trillion weavings where even the birth and death of entire Scales are but the frantic flickering of a candle against the encroaching dark."
The cube rotated through another configuration as Sadakar continued.

"You stand before me claiming the mantle of a lover of peace, Naldine Manthon, yet you stride into this sanctuary, into MY Sanctuary trailing the scent of inevitable ruin. Your very presence here serves as the first heavy precursor that will likely shatter the silence we have cultivated across eons of patient stillness."
A pause that seemed to last longer than it should have.
"But let us set aside your treaties and the fraying edges of your foresight for a moment."
The singularity’s attention fixed entirely on Noah now.
"The Infinity-bearer. I do not suppose you will tell this old existence just where you truly emerged from and how you possess the capability you hold?"
The question pressed against him with genuine curiosity.

"A great deal of things about you are undeniably curious. Which hidden realm did you form in? During which forgotten eon was your consciousness first sparked? What impossible materials of differentiation and undifferentiation composed the core of your existence to allow such a vessel to hold what you hold?"
Sadakar’s brilliance pulsed with each question.
"There are a great many questions about you. If you share, perhaps the old monsters trying to get their hands on you will simply sit back after they know."
What realm did he form in? What materials composed him?

Noah did not know how to tell this being that he was a simple human carried in a womb for nine months, born a weak baby that had to have his diapers changed every time he soiled himself. His mother had fed him milk and burped him over her shoulder. His mother had taught him to walk by holding his hands while he stumbled across floors that seemed impossibly vast to infant perception!
That certainly was not the grand image of the entity conducting Infinity across Observable Existence.
He thought of how to reply to this being, how to frame origins that seemed laughably mundane compared to what Sadakar clearly expected to hear.
Before he could formulate his response...
DING!
A ringing sound echoed through the structure, cutting through the stellar atmosphere like a blade through silk. The sound made Naldine frown immediately.
A deep sigh echoed from the Singular Cognizance, resignation and irritation mixing in that ancient voice.
"What did I say? You came bearing the weavings of Chaos, Naldine Manthon."
The cube rotated faster as Sadakar’s attention shifted toward something beyond the structure’s walls.
"Because now, those you consider your enemies have arrived. The Peasant and Moloch have now also arrived at my door."

chapters.title: Chapter 5045: Hadean! I
paragraphs: Are Primordial Architects the Blessed Lifeforms of Observable Existence?

Some entities emerge from the collision of differentiation and undifferentiation as Undivided Ones. Others crystallize into Formless Terrors. Still others become the countless classifications that populate Observable Existence at every Scale and depth.
But Primordial Architects are born different.

They emerge already holding authority that others spend eons cultivating. Some manifest at THE First Scale with foundations so refined that reaching Absolute depths becomes inevitability rather than aspiration. Others appear directly at THE Second Scale, their existence already transformed into configurations that most beings cannot achieve regardless of how long they struggle toward transcendence.

What did they possess within their existence that others didn’t? What quality separated their emergence from the emergence of everything else? Were they favored by THE First Cause itself, or did some random arrangement of forces during their formation grant them advantages that had nothing to do with preference?
Nobody knows.
The Primordial Architects themselves don’t know. They simply are what they are, born into privilege that they did nothing to earn and cannot explain to those who ask.
There was a time when THE Creature counted himself among them.

Before he became what he is now, before he shattered classifications and rebuilt himself into something that defied every category Observable Existence had established, he walked as a Primordial Architect.
His power was immense. His authority was absolute within the domains he claimed. His future stretched before him with possibilities that most beings could only dream of reaching.
And he chose to throw it all away.

The story goes that a Proterozoic Scale Primordial Architect stood before him when he announced his intention. An ancient entity whose name has been deliberately forgotten, someone who had watched THE Creature’s rise with concern.

"You understand this is irreversible," that entity had said. "What you propose is annihilation of everything you currently are. The weavings of a Primordial Architect cannot be reclaimed once abandoned. You will become nothing, and from that nothing, you hope to become something else entirely."
The entity paused, letting the severity settle.

"Things will forever change. You will never again be what you are now. The weavings that made you will dissolve, and whatever emerges from its ashes may not survive the process. You may entirly collapse and lose our blessing. Is that truly what you want?"
THE Creature’s response had been grand.

"A Blessing?" He laughed, and the sound made reality itself flinch. "You call this a Blessing? I call it a ceiling. I call it a cage with comfortable walls. I call it the highest room in a structure when I want to stand beneath open sky."
He had stepped forward, and even that ancient Primordial Architect had stepped back.

"Why I would leave behind such weavings? I ask you why I would keep them? To remain what I was born as? To accept limitations written into my existence before I had any say in what I would become? To spend eternity as the greatest version of something I never chose to be?"
His presence pressed against everything nearby, already beginning the process of unmaking what he had been.

"I don’t want to be a decent Primordial Architect. I want to be something that makes the very concept of Primordial Architects seem small. And if that means burning away every advantage I was given, then I will burn gladly. I...will always burn."
He smiled then, and he began to burn.

And THE Creature emerged from the ashes of what he abolished, standing as proof that chosen paths could exceed gifted ones, that will could surpass circumstance, that sometimes the greatest power came not from what you were given but from what you were willing to destroy in pursuit of what you wanted to become.
The Primordial Architects remained Blessed.
THE Creature...became something else entirely.
Erwin looked at the domain materializing before them as he and Moloch crossed into spaces hidden between the Observable and Unobservable.
"What is this place?" he asked the Singular Cognizance floating beside him. "And why did we come here?"
Moloch’s golden plates spun faster as they approached the main gate.

"Nakatsukuni. A unique Singular Cognizance and multiple Proterozoic Scale Architects have this domain as their home. They’ve maintained peace here for eons while the rest of Observable Existence tears itself apart with schemes and conflicts."
Erwin considered this information. Peaceful Proterozoic Scale beings seemed like a contradiction, but existence had shown him stranger things.
"And we’re here because?"
"Because you need to make some new friends."Moloch’s voice carried amusement that pressed against Erwin’s awareness.
"These are the hardest friends to make. Beings who have rejected conflict, who have chosen stillness over ambition, who will not be swayed by promises of power or threats of destruction."
The Singular Cognizance turned its attention fully toward Erwin.
"So we start with the hardest ones first. If you can convince those who want nothing to align with your cause, convincing everyone else becomes simple by comparison."
Erwin smiled at the logic. It was paradoxical in its own way, seeking allies among those least likely to become allies.

They entered through the main gate, passing Primordial Architects at Absolute depths who regarded them with expressions mixing wariness and curiosity. Erwin felt their gazes tracking him as he moved deeper into the compound, but he paid them little attention.
His focus was elsewhere.

His paradox burned within him with intensity that surprised even himself. The weavings of contradiction he had cultivated across eons reached a precipice now, pressing against boundaries that many may not have anticipated he could approach. His Civilizational Anchor was nearly complete. His claim to Paradox, held and not held simultaneously, pulsed with authority that made the Primordial Architects around him shift uncomfortably.
He was close now.

So very close to something that would change everything. But he was also even more cautious as he knew the closer one came to a grand accomplishment, the more likely they could fall and stumble. He had fallen and stumbled many times that he was now very careful of this. He wanted to see what would rise to try and trip him this time.

Still others become the countless classifications that populate Observable Existence at every Scale and depth.

They emerge already holding authority that others spend eons cultivating.
Some manifest at THE First Scale with foundations so refined that reaching Absolute depths becomes inevitability rather than aspiration.
Others appear directly at THE Second Scale, their existence already transformed into configurations that most beings cannot achieve regardless of how long they struggle toward transcendence.
What did they possess within their existence that others didn’t?
What quality separated their emergence from the emergence of everything else?
Were they favored by THE First Cause itself, or did some random arrangement of forces during their formation grant them advantages that had nothing to do with preference?
Nobody knows.
The Primordial Architects themselves don’t know.
They simply are what they are, born into privilege that they did nothing to earn and cannot explain to those who ask.
There was a time when THE Creature counted himself among them.

Before he became what he is now, before he shattered classifications and rebuilt himself into something that defied every category Observable Existence had established, he walked as a Primordial Architect.
His power was immense.
His authority was absolute within the domains he claimed.
His future stretched before him with possibilities that most beings could only dream of reaching.
And he chose to throw it all away.
The story goes that a Proterozoic Scale Primordial Architect stood before him when he announced his intention.
An ancient entity whose name has been deliberately forgotten, someone who had watched THE Creature’s rise with concern.
"You understand this is irreversible," that entity had said.
"What you propose is annihilation of everything you currently are.
The weavings of a Primordial Architect cannot be reclaimed once abandoned.
You will become nothing, and from that nothing, you hope to become something else entirely."
The entity paused, letting the severity settle.
"Things will forever change.
You will never again be what you are now.
The weavings that made you will dissolve, and whatever emerges from its ashes may not survive the process.
You may entirly collapse and lose our blessing.
Is that truly what you want?"
THE Creature’s response had been grand.
"A Blessing?" He laughed, and the sound made reality itself flinch.
"You call this a Blessing?
I call it a ceiling.
I call it a cage with comfortable walls.
I call it the highest room in a structure when I want to stand beneath open sky."
He had stepped forward, and even that ancient Primordial Architect had stepped back.
"Why I would leave behind such weavings?
I ask you why I would keep them?
To remain what I was born as?
To accept limitations written into my existence before I had any say in what I would become?
To spend eternity as the greatest version of something I never chose to be?"
His presence pressed against everything nearby, already beginning the process of unmaking what he had been.
"I don’t want to be a decent Primordial Architect.
I want to be something that makes the very concept of Primordial Architects seem small.
And if that means burning away every advantage I was given, then I will burn gladly.
I...will always burn."
He smiled then, and he began to burn.

And THE Creature emerged from the ashes of what he abolished, standing as proof that chosen paths could exceed gifted ones, that will could surpass circumstance, that sometimes the greatest power came not from what you were given but from what you were willing to destroy in pursuit of what you wanted to become.
The Primordial Architects remained Blessed.
THE Creature...became something else entirely.
Erwin looked at the domain materializing before them as he and Moloch crossed into spaces hidden between the Observable and Unobservable.
"What is this place?" he asked the Singular Cognizance floating beside him.
"And why did we come here?"
Moloch’s golden plates spun faster as they approached the main gate.
"Nakatsukuni.
A unique Singular Cognizance and multiple Proterozoic Scale Architects have this domain as their home.
They’ve maintained peace here for eons while the rest of Observable Existence tears itself apart with schemes and conflicts."
Erwin considered this information.
Peaceful Proterozoic Scale beings seemed like a contradiction, but existence had shown him stranger things.
"And we’re here because?"
"Because you need to make some new friends."Moloch’s voice carried amusement that pressed against Erwin’s awareness.
"These are the hardest friends to make.
Beings who have rejected conflict, who have chosen stillness over ambition, who will not be swayed by promises of power or threats of destruction."
The Singular Cognizance turned its attention fully toward Erwin.
"So we start with the hardest ones first.
If you can convince those who want nothing to align with your cause, convincing everyone else becomes simple by comparison."
Erwin smiled at the logic.
It was paradoxical in its own way, seeking allies among those least likely to become allies.
They entered through the main gate, passing Primordial Architects at Absolute depths who regarded them with expressions mixing wariness and curiosity.
Erwin felt their gazes tracking him as he moved deeper into the compound, but he paid them little attention.
His focus was elsewhere.
His paradox burned within him with intensity that surprised even himself.
The weavings of contradiction he had cultivated across eons reached a precipice now, pressing against boundaries that many may not have anticipated he could approach.
His Civilizational Anchor was nearly complete.
His claim to Paradox, held and not held simultaneously, pulsed with authority that made the Primordial Architects around him shift uncomfortably.
He was close now.
So very close to something that would change everything.
But he was also even more cautious as he knew the closer one came to a grand accomplishment, the more likely they could fall and stumble.
He had fallen and stumbled many times that he was now very careful of this.
He wanted to see what would rise to try and trip him this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 5046: Hadean! II
paragraphs: In THE Infiniverse.
In THE Seed of Observable Existence.
Noah lay alone on the golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore, his body stretched across ground that held warmth despite the rain falling upon it.

Multicolored droplets descended from heights that seemed infinite, each one carrying Quintessence Infiniforce that sank into his skin and dissolved into his foundations. The sensation was pleasant, like being bathed in potential rather than struggling to contain it.
Nobody was here.

His mother had stayed with THE Mnemonic Leviathan in its lava pools. His people trained in THE Yggdrheim or spread across the Three Thousand Realms exploring what THE Hadean Emergence had created. For the first time in what felt like ages, Noah found himself completely alone with nothing but rain and sand and the weight of everything Naldine had told him.
He didn’t smile when no one was watching.

Not because fear gripped him. Not because doubt crept in. Simply because smiling was sometimes for an audience, and right now there was none. His expression settled into something neutral as he processed the information he’d gathered.
Rhyacian, Calymmian, Ediacaran. Three tiers of Proterozoic Scale existence, each one containing beings who could crush him with effort ranging from moderate to none.
The enemies ahead were terrifying. He knew this with the same certainty he knew his own name.

But knowing the scope of what opposed him didn’t shake his resolve. It sharpened it. He knew that Naldine seemed to think his conviction bordered on delusion, that he smiled in the face of danger because certainty filled him so completely that reality couldn’t touch it.
She was partially right. He did possess conviction. He did believe he would find ways to overcome what stood before him.
The difference was that his conviction came from necessity rather than blind faith.

He simply couldn’t fail. Failure meant his mother dissolving into nothing. Failure meant Henry and Adelaide and everyone else he’d gathered being erased by forces they couldn’t resist. Failure meant everything he’d built collapsing, and Noah had built too much to watch it fall.
So he wouldn’t fail.
Not because Existence guaranteed his success. Fucking hell, sometimes, it felt like existence was working against him actively.

He wouldn’t fail because he refused to allow it. Every scheme, every preparation, every conversation with beings like Naldine who held knowledge he needed, all of it served a singular purpose. He would become strong enough that failure stopped being possible.
That was his conviction. Not certainty, but a glorious unshakableWill.
Multicolored rain continued falling on his face.

Noah closed his eyes and felt his existence, really felt it in ways he rarely took time to do. The vibrant drops landed on his skin and sank deeper, Quintessence Infiniforce merging with foundations that had already absorbed more Infinity than most beings could imagine. And hey, he hadn’t gone mad yet!
He thought about everything Naldine had shared during their journey.

The force of Observable and Unobservable that Proterozoic Scale entities pulled into themselves. That was their methodology when Infinity remained beyond reach. They drew from everything that could be perceived and everything that couldn’t, integrating those vast forces into Civilizations transformed to receive them.
But he had something different.

The force of Quintessence Infiniforce. The force of THE Infiniverse itself. When his domain had triggered THE Hadean Emergence and become a Seed of Observable Existence, something had begun flowing through their connection into him.
Not just pure power. Structure. Authority accumulated across Three Thousand Realms pressing into his finite existence through bonds that made separation impossible.
He finally understood what had been happening to his body.

Proterozoic Scale beings pulled the force of Observable into themselves at THE Second Scale. They channeled it carefully over eons, forging Proterozoic Organs and Bones from integrated authority that transformed what they were into what they needed to become.
He wasn’t at THE Proterozoic Scale.

But he had the force of an entire Seed of Observable Existence flowing into him right now. THE Infiniverse contained Three Thousand Realms of Quintessence, seas of combined authority, atmospheres of Primal Power that saturated everything within her boundaries. All of that connected to him. All of that pressed against his foundations through their unbreakable bond.
And most of it flowed toward one specific point within his existence.
His Organ of Civilization.

That aspect of his foundations had been undergoing change since THE Hadean Emergence completed. He’d felt it shifting, transforming, becoming something other than what it had been. The pressure concentrated there as if his Organ of Civilization was most receptive to what THE Infiniverse provided.
Noah opened his eyes and stared up at the multicolored rain descending toward him.

He knew what this force could potentially make possible. If Proterozoic Scale beings forged Proterozoic Organs from integrated Observable or Unobservable authority, then what could he forge from integrated Quintessence Infiniforce and the power of a Seed? The implications suggested capability that shouldn’t exist at his current Scale.

He focused on his Organ of Civilization and felt it respond to his attention. The transformation happening there had been passive until now, occurring without his direct involvement. But passive transformation meant passive results.
He didn’t want passive results.
"O Infinity."
His voice emerged quiet against the sound of falling rain.
"O Quintessence Infiniforce. O that which is Observable and Unobservable in THE Infiniverse."

The words felt right in ways he couldn’t explain. They were invitation and permission. Encouragement for processes already occurring to complete themselves according to his will rather than random chance.
"Flow freely. Let the Organ of Civilization bloom."
The Early Veiled Shore shook around him.

Noah felt the sand vibrating beneath his back, golden grains trembling as something responded to his declaration. The multicolored rain intensified, droplets falling faster and heavier as if THE Infiniverse itself heard his request and answered with enthusiasm. Pressure built within his existence, concentrated on that single point where his Organ of Civilization waited.
He knew Proterozoic Scale entities forged Proterozoic Organs or Bones. That was their methodology. That was their path.
But he wasn’t a Proterozoic Scale entity.
He was something else entirely. Something that had never existed before. Something that held Infinity in ways that defied classification while remaining at heights that shouldn’t permit such holding.
The prompt bloomed before his vision with brilliance that made the rain seem dim.
|Transformation Detected|

|Your Organ of Civilization has begun responding to accumulated authority from THE Seed of Observable Existence. The force of Quintessence Infiniforce combined with Observable and Unobservable weavings from the Three Thousand Realms has reached critical density within your foundations.|
|This transformation does not follow Proterozoic methodology.|
|This transformation follows no recorded methodology.|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization is emerging within your Existence.|
Noah lay on golden sand as multicolored rain fell upon him, his eyes fixed on words that declared something unprecedented was being born inside his foundations.
His smile returned.
This time, it was genuine. It was grand! It was...magisterial!

chapters.title: Chapter 5047: Hadean! III
paragraphs: The transformation was unique in ways Noah hadn’t anticipated.

His Organ of Civilization, which was becoming THE Hadean Organ of Civilization, kept moving across his body in patterns that defied prediction. From his head to his heart to his limbs and all extremities, the organ traveled as if searching for its proper home. He felt like a pinball machine, the transforming organ bouncing between locations while leaving trails of multicolored warmth wherever it passed.
He had to rise up from the golden sands.

The warmth of both the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity and THE Hadean Emergence bathed his body on all sides, two Miniature Causes working in harmony to saturate his existence with authority he’d helped create. The golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore around him had risen up and were floating like glimmers of golden stars, each grain suspended by forces responding to the transformation occurring within him.
Inside his body, as all of this took place, he continued to generate endless Quintessence Infiniforce.
All of it was a flood of sensations that he frankly had to say felt better than some of the grandest sensations he’d experienced so far in existence.
The pleasure wasn’t merely physical. It ran deeper, touching aspects of his foundations. Every moment of the transformation brought waves of something approaching bliss!
It even exceeded his euphoria during his spar with THE Creature.
That spar told him a great deal of things about existence itself. There was no need to say who was the victor of that spar, of course. After all, it was just a spar, right?
Right!
There was no need to declare a loser or a winner when both parties walked away with what they wanted!

What he did learn was that THE Creature’s power was unique beyond measure. Even though their confrontation occurred eons in the past from his perspective, THE Creature had felt just as strong if not stronger than the current version Noah had talked to in Alfheimr. That ancient monster had been playing with Adversity for longer than Noah could properly calculate, experimenting with concepts that most beings couldn’t comprehend.
But after fighting against him, Noah could effectively say that in all of existence, there likely wasn’t a single entity at THE First Scale who could possibly push him around.

If there was a competition for who the strongest entity below THE Proterozoic Scale was, he was fairly confident he’d be taking that title. With his control over Infinity externally, and now his control over Quintessence Infiniforce internally, paired with the budding and terrifying force of THE Infiniverse, the only thing he was currently looking forward to was punching upward toward entities on an entirely different Scale.
It felt like the change of the Organ of Civilization would aid with that endeavor.
HUUM!
As he was thinking this, he gained a profound new sense from the organ.

It felt like an extension of his being in ways his previous Organ of Civilization never had. Something within it had shifted, gaining an invisible force that pressed against his awareness with intensity that demanded acknowledgment. At this moment, he felt it begin to shine with multicolored crystalline light that pushed outward from within his chest.
The organ had stopped at the very center of his chest.
It had found its home.
The moment it completed its transformation...
BOOM!

Noah’s figure rose into the air involuntarily, lifted by forces responding to what had just emerged within him. The golden sand that had been floating around him began to spin in configurations that placed him at the absolute center, each grain orbiting his form as if he was the core of a galaxy being born. Light poured from his chest in streams of multicolored brilliance that painted the Early Veiled Shore in hues existence rarely witnessed.
As utmost glory spun around him, his chest began to shine even brighter.
From it began to rise a weapon.

A multicolored resplendent crystalline spear emerged from his sternum, pushing through flesh that parted without pain, materializing into physical form as it left his body. The weapon was a Kontos spear, its shaft stretching longer than cavalry lances, designed for reach and devastating strikes from positions of superiority. The crystalline material comprising it shifted through every color contained within Quintessence Infiniforce, never settling on a single hue, constantly flowing through the spectrum in patterns.

The spearhead itself was leaf-shaped and broad, edges sharp enough that looking at them seemed to cut perception. Runes he didn’t recognize covered the shaft in spiraling configurations, each one pulsing with light that matched the rhythm of his heartbeat. The butt of the spear ended in a crystalline counterweight that balanced the weapon perfectly despite its impossible length.
After it emerged fully and floated above Noah’s chest, he raised his hand to grasp it.
Everything around him began to tremble.

The Early Veiled Shore shook. The Three Thousand Realms beyond shook. THE Infiniverse itself seemed to recognize what had just been born within its creator’s existence. Noah’s fingers closed around the shaft of the spear, and the moment contact was made, prompts bloomed before his vision.
|Weapon Manifestation Complete|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization has allowed the emergence of THE Hadean Spear of Civilization.|
|THE HADEAN SPEAR OF CIVILIZATION|
|Classification: Civilizational Armament|

|Origin: First weapon to emerge from THE Hadean Organ of Civilization. Manifested through the transformation of the Organ within THE Youngest, bearer of Infinity and master of THE Seed of Observable Existence.|

|Description: A Kontos-style crystalline spear composed of solidified Quintessence Infiniforce merged with Observable and Unobservable weavings from THE Infiniverse. The weapon exists as an extension of its wielder’s transformed Organ of Civilization rather than a separate construct.|

|This Spear of Civilization holds the entire force of what is Observable and Unobservable within THE Infiniverse, multiplied by a factor of ten, then raised by an exponent of three. The resulting force contained within this weapon cannot be calculated.|

|Wielder Restriction: The only existence capable of bearing this Spear of Civilization is the one who holds THE Hadean Organ of Civilization. All others will find the spear impossible to lift regardless of their accumulated authority. The force contained within would crush any foundations lacking the specific transformation required to bear it.|

|WARNING: The force contained within this weapon is extremely heavy. Exercise caution regarding where you direct the tip of this spear. It is not recommended to point it toward anything at THE First Scale unless you wish to see their complete decimation. Their Civilizations will collapse. Their foundations will dissolve. Their existence will end before they comprehend what struck them.|

|Effectiveness against beings at THE Second Scale of Existence has not been determined.Testing against Proterozoic Scale entities is recommended before relying on this weapon in genuine conflict at those heights.|

Noah grasped THE Hadean Spear of Civilization and felt like he’d gained a truly terrifying extension of his power. The force within it pressed against his palm with intensity that would have atomized his hand before his transformation. Now it felt right. Heavy, but manageable. Devastating, but controllable.
But he knew that even this was only the cusp of the iceberg for his Organ of Civilization.

He could sense what was happening inside of it now, perceive aspects of his internal existence that had been hidden before the transformation. There were even grander changes occurring within, configurations that the spear’s emergence had only begun to reveal.
Inside his Organ of Civilization was the internal prison he’d created long ago.
THE Infinite Desmoterion.
He’d sent his own alternate body and identity there, Ozymandias, that hunger-driven portion of himself that he’d separated to cultivate independently.

Alongside Ozymandias waited the trash, repulsive, misshapen, good for nothing, useless foul waste of an Absolute who was THE Living Elemental, among other prisoners whose Civilizations he benefited from.
As their Civilizations arose, so would his. That was the nature of the prison he’d designed.
The transformation of the Organ of Civilization had affected this prison immensely.
New prompts bloomed before his vision.
|Internal Domain Transformation Detected|

|Due to the emergence of THE Hadean Organ of Civilization, an entire Civilizational Eon of Development has been carried out across THE Hadean Desmoterion. All prisoners within have experienced large jumps in power as time dilation paired with changes within the prison accelerated beyond previous parameters.|
|Progress notes of one prisoner in particular have been pulled forth for review.|
|PRISONER PROGRESS NOTES: OZYMANDIAS|
|Identity: Alternate existence of Master, separated and imprisoned for independent cultivation|
|Civilization: Infinite Hunger|
|Progress During Civilizational Eon of Development:|

|Phase One: Ozymandias achieved Uncountable Infinity across all depths of Absolute Sovereignty within the Civilization of Infinite Hunger. This process consumed approximately half of the Civilizational Eon.|

|Phase Two: The remaining half of the Civilizational Eon was spent reinforcing and saturating existence with Quintessence Infiniforce and the force of Observable and Unobservable weavings that have permeated across THE Hadean Organ of Civilization. Foundations have been thoroughly transformed.|
|Current Status:Ozymandias has reached the absolute peak of THE First Scale of Existence. No further advancement is possible without transitioning to THE Second Scale.|
|Recommendation:It is now possible for Ozymandias to establish a Civilizational Anchor to grasp identity as a Proterozoic Scale entity. All prerequisites have been met. The path forward is open.|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization has currently generated one additional usage of a Civilizational Eon of Development.|
|Shall this usage be utilized to take this alternate portion of your existence to THE Proterozoic Scale?|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization has transformed sufficiently to allow the release of prisoners within for a maximum duration of ten seconds, available once per hour.|

Noah floated in the air above the Early Veiled Shore, golden sand orbiting him like a galaxy, THE Hadean Spear of Civilization gripped in his hand, prompts declaring capabilities he hadn’t anticipated stretching before his vision.

Ozymandias had reached the peak of THE First Scale. That alternate portion of himself, cultivating independently within his prison, had achieved everything THE First Scale could offer. And now a choice presented itself.
Should he use the Civilizational Eon of Development to push Ozymandias into THE Proterozoic Scale?
A portion of himself at THE Second Scale while the rest remained at THE First.
Noah smiled as he looked at the spear in his hand.
THE Proterozoic Scale loomed ahead!.

The golden sand that had been floating around him began to spin in configurations that placed him at the absolute center, each grain orbiting his form as if he was the core of a galaxy being born.
Light poured from his chest in streams of multicolored brilliance that painted the Early Veiled Shore in hues existence rarely witnessed.
As utmost glory spun around him, his chest began to shine even brighter.
From it began to rise a weapon.
A multicolored resplendent crystalline spear emerged from his sternum, pushing through flesh that parted without pain, materializing into physical form as it left his body.
The weapon was a Kontos spear, its shaft stretching longer than cavalry lances, designed for reach and devastating strikes from positions of superiority.
The crystalline material comprising it shifted through every color contained within Quintessence Infiniforce, never settling on a single hue, constantly flowing through the spectrum in patterns.
The spearhead itself was leaf-shaped and broad, edges sharp enough that looking at them seemed to cut perception.
Runes he didn’t recognize covered the shaft in spiraling configurations, each one pulsing with light that matched the rhythm of his heartbeat.
The butt of the spear ended in a crystalline counterweight that balanced the weapon perfectly despite its impossible length.
After it emerged fully and floated above Noah’s chest, he raised his hand to grasp it.
Everything around him began to tremble.
The Early Veiled Shore shook.
The Three Thousand Realms beyond shook.
THE Infiniverse itself seemed to recognize what had just been born within its creator’s existence.
Noah’s fingers closed around the shaft of the spear, and the moment contact was made, prompts bloomed before his vision.
|Weapon Manifestation Complete|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization has allowed the emergence of THE Hadean Spear of Civilization.|
|THE HADEAN SPEAR OF CIVILIZATION|
|Classification: Civilizational Armament|
|Origin: First weapon to emerge from THE Hadean Organ of Civilization.
Manifested through the transformation of the Organ within THE Youngest, bearer of Infinity and master of THE Seed of Observable Existence.|
|Description: A Kontos-style crystalline spear composed of solidified Quintessence Infiniforce merged with Observable and Unobservable weavings from THE Infiniverse.
The weapon exists as an extension of its wielder’s transformed Organ of Civilization rather than a separate construct.|
|This Spear of Civilization holds the entire force of what is Observable and Unobservable within THE Infiniverse, multiplied by a factor of ten, then raised by an exponent of three.
The resulting force contained within this weapon cannot be calculated.|
|Wielder Restriction: The only existence capable of bearing this Spear of Civilization is the one who holds THE Hadean Organ of Civilization.
All others will find the spear impossible to lift regardless of their accumulated authority.
The force contained within would crush any foundations lacking the specific transformation required to bear it.|
|WARNING: The force contained within this weapon is extremely heavy.
Exercise caution regarding where you direct the tip of this spear.
It is not recommended to point it toward anything at THE First Scale unless you wish to see their complete decimation.
Their Civilizations will collapse.
Their foundations will dissolve.
Their existence will end before they comprehend what struck them.|

|Effectiveness against beings at THE Second Scale of Existence has not been determined.Testing against Proterozoic Scale entities is recommended before relying on this weapon in genuine conflict at those heights.|
Noah grasped THE Hadean Spear of Civilization and felt like he’d gained a truly terrifying extension of his power.
The force within it pressed against his palm with intensity that would have atomized his hand before his transformation.
Now it felt right.
Heavy, but manageable.
Devastating, but controllable.
But he knew that even this was only the cusp of the iceberg for his Organ of Civilization.
He could sense what was happening inside of it now, perceive aspects of his internal existence that had been hidden before the transformation.
There were even grander changes occurring within, configurations that the spear’s emergence had only begun to reveal.
Inside his Organ of Civilization was the internal prison he’d created long ago.
THE Infinite Desmoterion.
He’d sent his own alternate body and identity there, Ozymandias, that hunger-driven portion of himself that he’d separated to cultivate independently.

Alongside Ozymandias waited the trash, repulsive, misshapen, good for nothing, useless foul waste of an Absolute who was THE Living Elemental, among other prisoners whose Civilizations he benefited from.
As their Civilizations arose, so would his.
That was the nature of the prison he’d designed.
The transformation of the Organ of Civilization had affected this prison immensely.
New prompts bloomed before his vision.
|Internal Domain Transformation Detected|
|Due to the emergence of THE Hadean Organ of Civilization, an entire Civilizational Eon of Development has been carried out across THE Hadean Desmoterion.
All prisoners within have experienced large jumps in power as time dilation paired with changes within the prison accelerated beyond previous parameters.|
|Progress notes of one prisoner in particular have been pulled forth for review.|
|PRISONER PROGRESS NOTES: OZYMANDIAS|
|Identity: Alternate existence of Master, separated and imprisoned for independent cultivation|
|Civilization: Infinite Hunger|
|Progress During Civilizational Eon of Development:|
|Phase One: Ozymandias achieved Uncountable Infinity across all depths of Absolute Sovereignty within the Civilization of Infinite Hunger.
This process consumed approximately half of the Civilizational Eon.|

|Phase Two: The remaining half of the Civilizational Eon was spent reinforcing and saturating existence with Quintessence Infiniforce and the force of Observable and Unobservable weavings that have permeated across THE Hadean Organ of Civilization.
Foundations have been thoroughly transformed.|
|Current Status:Ozymandias has reached the absolute peak of THE First Scale of Existence.
No further advancement is possible without transitioning to THE Second Scale.|
|Recommendation:It is now possible for Ozymandias to establish a Civilizational Anchor to grasp identity as a Proterozoic Scale entity.
All prerequisites have been met.
The path forward is open.|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization has currently generated one additional usage of a Civilizational Eon of Development.|
|Shall this usage be utilized to take this alternate portion of your existence to THE Proterozoic Scale?|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization has transformed sufficiently to allow the release of prisoners within for a maximum duration of ten seconds, available once per hour.|

Noah floated in the air above the Early Veiled Shore, golden sand orbiting him like a galaxy, THE Hadean Spear of Civilization gripped in his hand, prompts declaring capabilities he hadn’t anticipated stretching before his vision.
Ozymandias had reached the peak of THE First Scale.
That alternate portion of himself, cultivating independently within his prison, had achieved everything THE First Scale could offer.
And now a choice presented itself.
Should he use the Civilizational Eon of Development to push Ozymandias into THE Proterozoic Scale?
A portion of himself at THE Second Scale while the rest remained at THE First.
Noah smiled as he looked at the spear in his hand.
THE Proterozoic Scale loomed ahead!.

chapters.title: Chapter 5048: Hadean! IV
paragraphs: <Unknown Record>
Very few knew who THE Youngest actually was across Observable Existence.
They heard stories. Whispers passed between beings who had witnessed fragments of his journey or felt the tremors of his Causes rippling through regions they called home.

They knew of him as the anomalous entity who wielded Infinity, the impossible existence who conducted endless authority seamlessly. His name circulated through the conversations of Primordial Architects and Singular Cognizances alike.
Most had never met him. Most were still looking for him.

They searched through Primordial Realms and hidden domains, following traces of Infinity that led nowhere, hunting an entity who moved faster than their schemes could track. They wanted to study him, use him, break him down into components they could understand and replicate. They spent time planning for a confrontation they assumed would go in their favor.
Then he began to pull out his spear.

Many would intimately come to know THE Youngest after that moment. They would learn exactly who he was and what he could do. They would understand, with perfect clarity, why the stories had failed to capture the truth of what he represented.
Their understanding lasted nanoseconds before the darkness of collapse overcame them.
Pity the souls that ever faced the end of that spear. Pity them, mourn them, and forget them. Because nothing remained of those existences worth remembering.
-Observation recorded in the aftermath ofTHE Hadean Decimations, author presumed dissolved
Noah grasped THE Hadean Spear of Civilization in his hand as he floated down gently toward the golden sands.

The grains cradled his figure when he landed, settling around his feet as if welcoming him back to solid ground. He put his other hand on his chest and sensed the terrifying pressure of THE Hadean Organ of Civilization pulsing within, its presence now unmistakable in ways it hadn’t been before the transformation. The organ had gained new capabilities.
The prison within him had changed.

Civilizational Eons of Development would now be generated through THE Hadean Organ of Civilization. One had already passed during the initial transformation, accelerating everything within THE Hadean Desmoterion beyond what normal time dilation could achieve. He had one more available. And he could utilize it to have his imprisoned self within him take that step and become a Second Scale existence.
With existence being so vast and full of terrors, this wasn’t something he would ever deny.
"Utilize the Civilizational Eon of Development."
He spoke the command lightly, as if ordering a meal rather than triggering a transformation that would reshape part of his own existence.
HUUM!
Prompts bloomed before his vision immediately.
|Command Accepted|
|The remaining Civilizational Eon of Development has been utilized.|

|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization is carrying out prolific, comprehensive, and quintessential advancement within THE Hadean Desmoterion. An entire eon will pass within the next ten seconds. Results will be displayed upon completion.|
|Time Remaining: 10 seconds|
Noah smiled brilliantly at the words.
Ten seconds out here. An entire eon in there. His other self would have lifetimes to accomplish what needed accomplishing while Noah barely had time to examine what he’d already gained.
He proceeded to grasp his spear properly and look at it while the seconds began to tick down.

The weapon felt light within his hands despite carrying the terrifying power of his Infiniverse’s Observable and Unobservable weavings multiplied by a factor of ten and then raised by an exponent of three.

The spear responded to his grip as if it weighed nothing at all. The crystalline shaft hummed against his palms, resonating with his heartbeat in ways that made him feel like the weapon had always been part of him.
He needed to get a feel for it.
Noah raised the spear above his head and swung it down once in a simple vertical arc.

The motion began slowly, almost lazily, the crystalline weapon cutting through air that suddenly felt thick with potential. As the spearhead descended, something emerged around the shaft that made Noah’s eyes widen with genuine surprise.
Two rivers of misty light began swirling around the weapon.

The first river was clear, almost invisible, perceptible only through the way it bent light around itself. It moved like smoke given purpose, coiling around the spear’s shaft in patterns that seemed to follow rules Noah couldn’t immediately identify.
This force felt cold in ways that had nothing to do with temperature, pressing against his awareness with the sensation of everything that existed beyond perception’s reach.
The Unobservable.

The second river blazed with golden luminosity that painted the Early Veiled Shore in hues of captured sunlight. It wound around the spear in configurations opposite to its clear counterpart, the two forces spiraling together without ever quite touching.
This force felt warm and present, the accumulated acknowledgment of everything that could be witnessed pressing outward with intensity that demanded recognition.
The Observable.

Both rivers danced around his descending spear as if existence itself had decided to manifest its fundamental division through his weapon. Clear and gold, hidden and seen, unknown and known, the two forces representing everything that Proterozoic Scale beings pulled into themselves to forge their transformations. He was watching the nature of Second Scale power made visible around a weapon that shouldn’t exist.
His seemingly simple swing stopped midway through its arc.
The rivers of clear and gold didn’t stop with it.
BOOM!
The force continued forward without the spear to guide it.

Utter devastation unfolded before Noah’s eyes as the golden sands in front of him split down the middle. A canyon carved itself into the Early Veiled Shore, reaching deeper than the sands should have extended, revealing layers of existence beneath that he’d never seen. The sacred waters of the shores ahead parted like curtains being drawn aside, liquid authority separating into two halves that continued moving apart as the force traveled beyond them.
Light years away, the shimmering barrier protecting the Early Veiled Shore from the rest of THE Infiniverse tore open!

The force of a single incomplete swing had crossed distances, ripping through protections designed to keep his farms safe from everything outside them. Beyond that barrier, Noah sensed the damage continuing, the rivers of Observable and Unobservable force pressing toward one of the Three Thousand Realms with momentum that showed no signs of stopping!
His expression went somber immediately.

Noah clenched his free hand and pulled, his will reaching out to grasp the escaping force and dissipate it before it could tear through an entire Realm he’d just created. The clear and golden rivers resisted for a moment, wanting to continue their path of destruction, before finally dissolving into harmless particles of light that scattered across the void.
He breathed out calmly and looked down at the terrifying weapon in his hand.

One swing. Not even a complete swing. Just the beginning of a vertical arc, stopped halfway through, and the resulting force had nearly destroyed a Realm while tearing across light years of distance. This was a catastrophe shaped like a spear, devastation given form that could be directed but would require extreme care to control!
As he was holding it, processing what had just happened, he began to feel something else.

His own body started emanating terrifying waves of power that pressed outward in pulses matching his heartbeat. His immensity, which he’d already thought was reaching unheard of heights, was rising even further. This change came from within, his Organ of Civilization pulsing with glory as something completed itself in THE Hadean Desmoterion.
The ten seconds had passed.
New prompts bloomed before his vision.
|Civilizational Eon of Development: Complete|
|Progress Report: OZYMANDIAS|
|Phase One: Civilizational Anchor Establishment|
|Duration: First half of Civilizational Eon|

|Ozymandias utilized his profound foundation, refined across the previous Civilizational Eon of Development, to establish his Civilizational Anchor. The absolute self-knowledge required for this process was achieved through introspection spanning centuries of dilated time. Every aspect of his existence was examined, understood, and crystallized into certainty that could not be shaken.|
|Result:Civilizational Anchor successfully established. Ozymandias has grasped THE Proterozoic Scale of Existence. Your alternate self now exists at THE Second Scale.|
|Phase Two: Proterozoic Transformation Attempt|
|Duration: Latter half of Civilizational Eon|

|With the Civilizational Anchor established, Ozymandias utilized the remaining time to attempt the formation of a Proterozoic Organ or Bone. Materials available within THE Hadean Desmoterion, combined with the Observable and Unobservable weavings permeating THE Hadean Organ of Civilization, were employed in this process.|
|Result: In Progress. Transformation has begun.|

|Your other self seeks for you to experience the changes directly. Ozymandias requests that you send your gaze into the prison and experience the eon of development through the memories accumulated during the process.|
|A Civilizational Eon’s worth of experiences awaits your review.|
Noah smiled brilliantly as he felt the terrifying changes resonating through his existence.

Due to the dilated time governing his prison, he could peek into the memories of Ozymandias whenever he chose to. Every moment of that eon, every struggle and breakthrough and revelation his other self had experienced, all of it waited for him to observe. He now had a Civilizational Eon’s worth of memories to sift through at his leisure.
More importantly, he could feel just what had happened to his other self.
Ozymandias had taken the step forward.
A portion of his existence now operated at THE Proterozoic Scale, and it felt...immense!
